headline: Sindh University organizes sports week
description: HYDERABAD - The Sports Week 2026, organised by the Faculty of Law, University of Sindh, successfully concluded with great enthusiasm and sporting spirit on
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: HYDERABAD - The Sports Week 2026, organised by the Faculty of Law, University of Sindh, successfully concluded with great enthusiasm and sporting spirit on Saturday. The SU’s spokesman Nadir Mugheri informed that a prize and certificate distribution ceremony was held later with Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Fateh Muhammad Marri (TI), distributing the certificates among the winning teams. Addressing the ceremony, he said participation in sports alongside academic activities was essential for students. He stated that achievements in sports were not limited to winning prizes but also instilled in students the values of hard work, dedication, discipline, tolerance and teamwork. He apprised that a mega Inter-Department Sports Gala would be organised at the university on November 10. According to Mugheri, various indoor and outdoor sports competitions were organised during the sports week.The competitions provided students with an excellent opportunity to showcase their sporting abilities while promoting teamwork, discipline, leadership and sportsmanship, he told.

headline: Rs36.8m disbursed under welfare schemes in Sukkur Range in 10 months
description: SUKKUR - DIG Sukkur Nasir Aftab has released a 10-month performance report of the Sukkur Range Police covering police welfare, shuhada welfare and other
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: SUKKUR - DIG Sukkur Nasir Aftab has released a 10-month performance report of the Sukkur Range Police covering police welfare, shuhada welfare and other matters in the three districts of the range: Sukkur, Khairpur Mirs and Ghotki. According to details on Saturday, under the supervision of Incharge Welfare Branch Assistant Muhammad Ibrahim Ansari and Lady Officer Shabana Yasmeen, timely assistance is being provided for resolving issues of the families of martyrs through the Shuhada Welfare Desk and Shuhada WhatsApp Group in Sukkur Range. A total of 565 cases were processed in time and an amount of Rs36,814,910 was paid to police officers and personnel, including Rs530,000 in 50 immediate relief fund cases, Rs11,409,554 in 221 retirement grant cases, Rs18,000,000 in 180 marriage grant cases and Rs2,105,356 in 114 medical charges cases. Furthermore, 195 cases of different categories were completed in time, including 09 cases of Shaheed compensation, 03 of injury compensation, 42 of financial assistance, 29 of reimbursement, 67 of group insurance, 34 of benevolent fund, 11 of scholarship cases, pension and final payment of GP Fund. A total of 4,412 beneficiaries, including 1,114 police officers and personnel and 3,298 members of their families, availed free medical treatment facilities from police panel hospitals in Sindh, including Hira Hospital, River City Hospital, Indus Hospital, Rahim Yar Khan Hospital, Mehran Medical Hospital, Kisan Clinic, Shahani Bone Care Hospital and Ziauddin Hospital. DIG Sukkur reiterated his resolve that the welfare of Shuhada-e-Sindh Police, officers and jawans of Sindh Police and their families is our top priority and instructions have been issued to the concerned officers and officials to resolve their problems in time. He said the efforts of the officers and personnel of the Welfare Branch in this regard are commendable and expressed hope that the Welfare Branch will continue to work for the welfare of the martyrs of Sindh Police, all employees of Sindh Police and their families with the same zeal and spirit in future.

headline: Anti-encroachment drive conducted along Auto Bhan Road
description: HYDERABAD - On the directives of Deputy Commissioner Hyderabad, Zain-ul-Aabdeen Memon, an anti-encroachment operation was conducted along Auto Bhan Road.
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: HYDERABAD - On the directives of Deputy Commissioner Hyderabad, Zain-ul-Aabdeen Memon, an anti-encroachment operation was conducted along Auto Bhan Road. The operation was carried out under the supervision of Assistant Commissioner Latifabad, Saud Ahmed, and the Mukhtiarkar of Latifabad, covering several locations including Pathan Goth, Unit No. 7, and the area in front of the Mehran Arts Council. The operation was carried out under supervision of Assistant Commissioner Latifabad, Saud Ahmed, and the Mukhtiarkar of Latifabad, covering several locations including Pathan Goth, Unit No. 7, and the area in front of the Mehran Arts Council. During the drive, trucks, parked vehicles, cabin-like structures, and other illegal obstructions situated within the designated limits of the newly constructed Auto Bhan Road were removed. The objective of the operation was to restore the road’s original boundaries, keep the public thoroughfare free from encroachments, and improve the flow of traffic. The district administration has made it clear that illegal occupation of, or encroachment upon, public roads and thoroughfares will not be permitted under any circumstances.

headline: BISE announces results of 9th class examinations
description: NAWABSHAH - Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Shaheed Benazirabad, with the approval of Chairman Dr. Asif Ali Memon, Controller of Examinations
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: NAWABSHAH - Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Shaheed Benazirabad, with the approval of Chairman Dr. Asif Ali Memon, Controller of Examinations Shah Muhammad Farooq Rashdi, has announced the results of Annual Examinations 2026 for Class IX Science and General Groups, conducted by the Board. According to results released by the Board, a total of 52,260 candidates registered for the Science Group examinations, out of whom 51,546 appeared. A total of 41,425 students were declared successful, with an overall pass percentage of 79.02 percent. The results further show that 41,425 candidates passed all subjects in the Science Group, while 4,353 candidates passed six subjects, 1,517 passed five subjects, 1,380 passed four subjects, 704 passed three subjects, 342 passed two subjects and 286 candidates managed to pass only one subject. Similarly, a total of 50 candidates registered for the General Group examinations, and all 50 appeared. Of these, 26 students were declared successful, recording an overall pass percentage of 52 percent. According to results, 10 candidates passed six subjects, two passed five subjects, four passed four subjects, one passed three subjects and one candidate passed two subjects. The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education stated that, in accordance with the decision of Government of Sindh’s Universities and Boards Department, a new grading system has been introduced for the Class IX (Part-I) annual examinations this year. Under the new system, candidates securing less than 40 percent marks will be declared “Ungraded” and will not be considered successful in the respective paper. According to Board officials, candidates can also check their results through the Board’s official website, www.bisesba.edu.pk, and its Android application.

headline: 90 day ban imposed on illegal hunting of wild birds in Sukkur
description: SUKKUR - Commissioner Sukkur, Abid Saleem Qureshi, on Saturday imposed a 90-day ban on hunting, trapping, netting and illegal firing of wild birds in all three
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: SUKKUR - Commissioner Sukkur, Abid Saleem Qureshi, on Saturday imposed a 90-day ban on hunting, trapping, netting and illegal firing of wild birds in all three districts of Sukkur division, including Sukkur, Khairpur and Ghotki, to protect wildlife and prevent illegal hunting of rare bird species. In this regard, a notification has been issued under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.PC), imposing the ban with effect from October 28, 2026. According to the notification, legal action will be taken against violators under Section 188 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), while the concerned police officers have also been authorized to register complaints for violations. The objective of this step is to ensure the protection of wildlife, survival of rare bird species and prevention of illegal hunting.

headline: Over 86,000 medicines integrated into track and trace system: Mustafa Kamal
description: KARACHI - Federal Minister for Health Mustafa Kamal has said that the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) has been made fully transparent and
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Federal Minister for Health Mustafa Kamal has said that the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) has been made fully transparent and digitalized. More than 86,000 medicines manufactured by the pharmaceutical industry have been registered under the Track and Trace System, enabling con-sumers to scan medicines easily through their mobile phones and verify their authenticity as well as obtain information about their prices. He said that pharmaceutical companies could also register their medicines and products online. A pro-cess that previously took years is now being completed within just 21 days. He expressed these views while addressing industrialists during his visit to the Korangi Association of Trade and Industry (KATI). The event was attended by KATI President Sheikh Umer Rehan, Deputy Patron-in-Chief Zubair Chhaya, Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM) leader Anis Qaimkhani, KITE Chairman Zahid Saeed, CEO Saleem-uz-Zaman, Senior Vice President Farukh Qandhari, Vice President Nasir Sheikh, former presidents and chairmen Gulzar Feroz and KATI members. The Federal Health Minister further stated that eight months had passed since DRAP’s certification procedures were shifted to a digital system, during which more than 5,000 cases had been processed. He added that, in recognition of this landmark initiative, the Prime Minister had awarded DRAP for its outstanding performance in digitalization. Mustafa Kamal said that he had performed his responsibilities with sincerity and a sense of duty, and the positive outcome was evident in the pharmaceutical industry’s current satisfaction. Recalling his tenure as Karachi’s City Nazim, he said that he had spent Rs. 300 billion on the city’s infrastructure, a contribution that continued to be remembered. The Federal Minister said that the issue of medicine pricing required serious attention. The pharma-ceutical industry was seeking an increase in medicine prices, but the matter was considered by the federal cabinet. He suggested that the government should withdraw from direct price regulation and allow medicine prices, like those of other products, to be determined by the open market. Mustafa Kamal further said that Karachi was not receiving its rightful share. Earlier, KATI President Sheikh Umer Rehan said that his association with Mustafa Kamal dated back several decades. When Mustafa Kamal first became Karachi’s City Nazim, his first official visit was to KATI. He maintained regular contact with the association and facilitated the construction of Road 8000. Sheikh Umer Rehan proposed that, on the pattern of the FBR Chairman, all federal ministers should visit Karachi at least once a month and address the concerns of stakeholders in their respective sec-tors. He said that Pakistan’s cost of production was among the highest in the region, yet the government had further increased the interest rate, adding to the challenges faced by industry. The KATI President said that the Korangi Industrial Area was home to a substantial share of the phar-maceutical industry, which was playing a key role in the country’s pharmaceutical sector. According to the statistics, pharmaceutical exports reached $457 million in FY2024-25, registering an increase of approximately 34 percent compared to the previous fiscal year.

headline: Sindh Home Minister orders enhanced security for Shahrah-e-Bhutto Expressway
description: KARACHI - Sindh Home Minister Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar has directed the relevant departments to review and strengthen the security arrangements for the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Sindh Home Minister Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar has directed the relevant departments to review and strengthen the security arrangements for the Shahrah-e-Bhutto Expressway, emphasising the need to develop the newly constructed road as a model expressway. He issued these directives while chairing a high-level meeting on the Shahrah-e-Bhutto Expressway Project, attended by senior government officials and police authorities. The Home Minister said the expressway was an important development project and that the Sindh Government was giving it special attention. He stressed that its security was of utmost importance and called for a fresh review of the existing security strategy and operational arrangements. Lanjar directed the concerned authorities to arrange two mobile mechanic vans at the earliest to assist motorists in case of vehicle breakdowns. He also ordered arrangements for towing vehicles to ensure prompt assistance to stranded motorists. He further directed the relevant departments to ensure proper marking of entry and exit points and other important locations along the expressway, besides taking necessary measures for the installa-tion of CCTV cameras. He said these cameras should be integrated into the Safe City Project/S-4 system. The Home Minister said the objective was to establish Shahrah-e-Bhutto Expressway as a model road, with similar infrastructure to be extended to other districts of the province in the future. Emphasising interdepartmental coordination, he said timely completion of development projects re-quired close cooperation among all relevant departments. He directed the concerned authorities to address administrative issues, identify challenges and pre-pare practical recommendations to ensure effective progress on the project. Sindh IGP informed the meeting that mobile patrolling was continuing round the clock to ensure the security of Shahrah-e-Bhutto Expressway. He added that Traffic Police, local police and Highway Police were actively performing their duties along the route. The IGP further stated that recommendations regarding the provision of required resources, modern equipment and vehicles would soon be forwarded to the Home Department. The meeting was attended by Special Assistant to the Chief Minister for Investment and Public-Private Partnership Projects Qasim Naveed Qamar, Secretaries of Finance, Transport and Local Government Departments, Additional Secretary Home, Additional IG Karachi, DIGs, officials of Traffic Police, High-way Police and East Zone, Tanveer Gadi, and other relevant officials.

headline: SECP marks over 39,000 non-filing companies inactive
description: ISLAMABAD - The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has marked 39,704 companies “Inactive by Registrar” after they failed to file
author: Imran Ali Kundi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has marked 39,704 companies “Inactive by Registrar” after they failed to file annual returns and/or financial statements for four years. Marking non-filing companies as inactive will make the corporate register more reliable and help prevent dormant companies from being misused.

The inactive status will appear in the SECP’s system and be visible to banks and other stakeholders. These companies will not be able to open new bank accounts until they file their overdue documents with the SECP and regain active status. They will also be unable to access financial services or register changes in their directors.

The inactive companies include 13,927 in Lahore, 13,859 in Islamabad, 4,868 in Karachi, 2,031 in Peshawar, 1,861 in Multan, 1,384 in Faisalabad, 1,102 in Gilgit, 436 in Quetta and 236 in Sukkur.

Filing annual returns and, where required, financial statements is a legal requirement under the Companies Act, 2017. These filings keep public information about companies, their ownership and their management up to date. The SECP said prolonged non-filing weakens the corporate register and can hinder efforts to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.

The corporate register continues to grow. Pakistan had 317,002 registered companies at the end of September 2026. The SECP registered 43,559 new companies in the previous financial year, 24 per cent more than the year before. Company name reservation and incorporation are now fully digital, and 99.9 per cent of new companies are registered online.

“A clean and credible registry is the bedrock of trust in the corporate sector. SECP is protecting the integrity of the financial system while giving companies a clear opportunity to return to compliance,” SECP Chairman Dr Kabir Ahmed Sidhu said.

headline: Anti-polio campaign inaugurated
description: KARACHI - Sindh Secretary Health Tahir Hussain Sangi has inaugurated November polio vaccination campaign at Khalid Jameel Dispensary, District East, Karachi,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Sindh Secretary Health Tahir Hussain Sangi has inaugurated November polio vaccination campaign at Khalid Jameel Dispensary, District East, Karachi, on Saturday. Nearly 6.8 million children to be vaccinated across 20 districts of Sindh from 2–8 November. Sindh Secretary Health Tahir Hussain Sangi has said that anti-polio vaccination available through door-to-door teams and fixed vaccination sites. He said that every child under five must be reached and protected against polio. “Our priority is to ensure no eligible child is missed during the November campaign”, Secretary Health said, adding that Sindh aims to interrupt poliovirus transmission within the coming year. He said that only one environmental sample was positive last month and six have tested positive this month. Increase in positive environmental samples calls for a vigorous vaccination response, he said adding “We must respond vigorously to interrupt transmission and protect every child from polio”. According to EOC Sindh, Sindh intensifying vaccination efforts as poliovirus is detected in environmental samples. Repeated polio vaccination is essential to build children’s immunity and stop transmission. Parents urged to vaccinate every child under five through visiting teams or fixed vaccination sites. The Government of Sindh is committed to protecting every child and contributing to a polio-free Pakistan.

headline: COP31 workshop explores green investment opportunities
description: KARACHI - A workshop aimed at exploring new investment opportunities to mitigate the effects of climate change and protect the environment held ahead of the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - A workshop aimed at exploring new investment opportunities to mitigate the effects of climate change and protect the environment held ahead of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Sindh Environment Secretary Faisal Ahmed Uqaili, Lahore High Court Justice Jawad Hassan, Karachi Centre for Climate Change founding director Bilal Sohail, and a large number of representatives from government institutions, the investment community, environmental experts and other relevant sectors attended the workshop. Participants held detailed discussions on various environmental initiatives, including access to clean water, restoration of agricultural land and orchards, reduction of industrial pollution and carbon emissions, promotion of electric vehicles and transparency in carbon projects. Opening the dialogue, K4C founding director Bilal Sohail stressed the need to translate Pakistan’s climate commitments into practical projects and investment opportunities. He said effective measures in the water, energy and carbon sectors, along with private-sector participation, were essential for an industrial and coastal city like Karachi. Lahore High Court Justice Jawad Hassan highlighted the importance of effective environmental legislation, protection of public interest and a clear regulatory framework to address climate change. He said legal certainty was essential to encourage private-sector investment, adding that laws and policies must ensure environmental protection while providing investors with clear guidance and confidence. Speaking on the occasion,Faisal Ahmed Uqaili outlined the Sindh government’s initiatives to address climate change, protect the environment and strengthen policymaking, institutional reforms and practical interventions.He said the provincial government had approved 13 carbon-market projects and forwarded them to the federal Ministry of Climate Change. These projects had the potential to reduce emissions equivalent to 330.13 million tonnes of carbon dioxide. The projects include wind power, emission reduction in the energy sector, production of biochar from agricultural waste, reduction of methane emissions and sustainable forestry initiatives. He added that the Sindh government had also prepared six priority climate projects worth $62.15 million. These include biogas projects in five districts, floating agriculture in lower Sindh, reduction of carbon emissions from brick kilns and capacity-building initiatives in climate finance. Uqaili said Sindh faced serious climate-related threats, including extreme heat, floods, water scarcity, rising sea levels and seawater intrusion into coastal areas. Addressing these challenges required joint efforts by the government, private sector and international development partners. He said Sindh’s provincial recommendations for the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0) had been prepared, while work was also under way on a digital climate registry and dashboard to monitor carbon emissions and assess the performance of climate projects. The secretary said the provincial government believed in guiding and supporting industrial development alongside enforcing environmental laws. In this regard, memorandums of understanding had also been signed with various educational institutions to promote research and collaboration. Participants appreciated the Sindh government’s environmental initiatives and policies and expressed hope that the province’s experience and measures would contribute towards positive progress in addressing climate change at COP31. The 31st Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC will be held in Antalya, Turkiye, from Nov 9 to 20, 2026. Heads of state, government representatives, experts and officials from relevant institutions from across the world are expected to attend. Pakistan will also present its national climate priorities and position at the conference, with representation from both federal and provincial governments. Discussions will focus on addressing the impacts of climate change, environmental protection, investment in climate projects, climate adaptation and strengthening international cooperation.

headline: Karachi Mayor inaugurates first World Culture Festival exhibition
description: KARACHI - Method and Madness, the first exhibition out of five planned during the World Culture Festival, was opened by Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab on Friday.
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Method and Madness, the first exhibition out of five planned during the World Culture Festival, was opened by Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab on Friday. After witnessing the artworks on view made by 12 international and 14 Pakistani artists, Mr Wahab spoke to the media and the artists at the Arts Council, Karachi. He welcomed them all to Karachi and hoped they would enjoy their stay in the city and their interaction with fellow artists. During the exhibition, speaking to media, Ireland’s ambassador to Pakistan Mary O’Neill said the at-mosphere at the event was super exciting. “It’s great to see artists from around the world.” Answering a question about the importance of holding such events at a time when the world is faced with conflicts, she said these events are important because they transcend circumstances. The festival has brought together around 1,000 international artists from more than 150 countries, alongside 500 Pakistani artists, transforming Karachi into a vibrant meeting point of world cultures. The 25-day festival, scheduled to be ended on Nov 22, offers an extraordinary platform for artists, per-formers, writers and creative communities from across the globe to share their cultural traditions, social norms, culinary practices, literary expressions and contemporary artistic trends. The World Culture Festival - Karachi 2026 features an extensive programme of music, theatre, dance, visual arts, films, workshops, live mural painting, fine arts sessions and interactive cultural discussions. Pakistani folk traditions, qawwali, contemporary music and theatrical productions are being presented alongside international performances, creating opportunities for artistic learning, collaboration and cross-cultural engagement. With artists and cultural representatives from more than 150 countries, the festival offers a remarkable opportunity to experience the diversity of human civilisation under one roof.

headline: Sri Lankan HC for stronger economic ties with Pakistan
description: LAHORE - Sri Lankan High Commissioner to Pakistan, Rear Admiral (r) Fred Senevirathne Saturday called for stronger trade and economic cooperation between
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LAHORE - Sri Lankan High Commissioner to Pakistan, Rear Admiral (r) Fred Senevirathne Saturday called for stronger trade and economic cooperation between Pakistan and Sri Lanka, stressing the need to translate the longstanding brotherly relations between the two countries into increased commercial engagement, investment and business partnerships.

He was talking to business community here at Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), where LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar gave a detailed overview of Pakistan’s economy while Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani and Vice President Chaudhry Khadim Hussain also spoke on the occasion.

The high commissioner invited Pakistani businessmen to explore the trade and investment opportunities available in Sri Lanka and develop closer commercial relationships with their Sri Lankan counterparts. He stressed the importance of strengthening economic engagement so that the friendly relations between the two countries could also produce greater benefits for their business communities. LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar said that Pakistan and Sri Lanka enjoy cordial and longstanding relations, which provided a strong foundation for expanding bilateral trade and economic cooperation. He said that both countries needed to make greater efforts to convert these friendly ties into practical business opportunities.

The LCCI president proposed the exchange of trade delegations between the two countries to help businessmen understand each other’s markets, identify potential partners and explore new avenues of cooperation. He also suggested organizing single-country exhibitions in Pakistan and Sri Lanka to showcase products, services and investment opportunities, enabling companies to establish direct business contacts.

He highlighted Lahore’s importance as a vibrant business and commercial center and a significant contributor to Pakistan’s exports. He said that stronger engagement with Sri Lankan businesses could open new avenues for Pakistani exporters and investors while providing opportunities for Sri Lankan companies to explore the Pakistani market.

He stressed the need to promote business-to-business (B2B) contacts and strengthen chamber-to-chamber relations, explaining that direct interaction between business organizations could help identify areas of mutual interest and develop lasting commercial partnerships. He also encouraged businessmen from both countries to explore opportunities for establishing business outlets in each other’s markets, which could help improve market access and strengthen commercial presence.

The LCCI president further underscored the importance of sustained interaction between the business communities, saying that regular exchanges, exhibitions and intra-chamber cooperation could play a meaningful role in expanding bilateral trade. He said that closer coordination between the chambers would help businesses identify practical opportunities and build stronger economic connections.

LCCI Senior Vice President Sardar Usman Ghani and Vice President Chaudhry Khadim Hussain also spoke on the occasion and exchanged views on strengthening Pakistan–Sri Lanka economic relations and promoting greater cooperation between the business communities.

Honorary Consul of Sri Lanka Yasin Joyia, former LCCI Vice Presidents Mian Zahid Javed and Haris Atiq, Members of the LCCI Executive Committee Huma Junaid, Shahzad Ali Shah, Muhammad Ali, Shahzad Mahmood, Mardan Ali Zaidi, Chaudhry Zulfiqar Ali, Amir Ata Barry, Syed Yousaf Jamil, Ali Raza, Adeel Babar Khan and Chaudhry Muhammad Fargham were also present.

headline: Gold price plummets by Rs10,800 per tola
description: ISLAMABAD - The price of gold witnessed a significant decline in the local market on Saturday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola falling by Rs10,800 to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The price of gold witnessed a significant decline in the local market on Saturday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola falling by Rs10,800 to settle at Rs 409,736, according to rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association. Similarly, the price of 10 grams of 24-karat gold decreased by Rs 9,259 to Rs 351,282, while 10 grams of 22-karat gold fell by Rs 8,487 to Rs 322,020. In the international market, the price of gold declined by $108 to $3,872 per ounce, the association reported.

Meanwhile, the price of silver per tola decreased by Rs 142 to Rs 5,388, while the price of 10 grams of silver fell by Rs 122 to Rs 4,619. The price of silver in the international market also declined by $1.42 to $49.10 per ounce, the association added.

headline: Court approves bail for Iqrar-ul-Hassan in NCCIA case
description: KARACH - A district court on Saturday approved the bail plea of Awam Raj Tehreek Chief Iqrar-ul-Hassan in a case involving the alleged dissemination of
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACH - A district court on Saturday approved the bail plea of Awam Raj Tehreek Chief Iqrar-ul-Hassan in a case involving the alleged dissemination of anti-state content on social media. The court ordered the journalist and former television host to submit surety bonds worth Rs 200,000. Earlier on October 22, 2026, the Judicial Magistrate-East had dismissed his bail application. On October 19, a judicial magistrate had sent Hassan to judicial remand after rejecting the NCCIA’s request for an extension of his physical remand. The agency had produced Hassan before the Judicial Magistrate-East and sought his physical remand in connection with allegations that he posted anti-state material on social media. However, the court rejected the request and directed the NCCIA to submit the challan within 14 days. According to details provided, Hassan was arrested in Lahore’s Defence Housing Authority (DHA) and subsequently brought to Karachi at around 1:00 AM.

headline: Sindh govt preparing master plans for 31 cities to ensure urban development
description: KARACHI - Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Saturday said that the provincial government was work-ing on master plans for 31 cities to ensure
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Saturday said that the provincial government was work-ing on master plans for 31 cities to ensure planned, sustainable and inclusive urban development, with Karachi and Hyderabad among the major cities whose plans were being prepared. Addressing the Sindh Cities Forum 2026, organised by Sindh Master Planning Authority (SMPA) in col-laboration with NED University and UN-Habitat to mark World Cities Day at Golf Club’s Convention Centre, the chief minister said master planning was essential to address the growing challenges of ur-banisation, including unplanned construction, traffic congestion, water shortages, inadequate drainage and the effects of climate change. According to the minister for local government, housing and town planning, master plans for 17 cities had been completed, while work on the remaining 14 was in its final stages. The government had so far issued notification for the master plans of nine cities: Sukkur, Larkana, Mirpurkhas, Umerkot, Mithi, Islamkot, Dadu, Nawabshah and Naushahro Feroze. The CM said work on the master plans for Karachi and Hyderabad was progressing rapidly. Internation-al consultants had been engaged for Karachi’s master plan, which, he acknowledged, would be a par-ticularly challenging exercise given the city’s existing urban conditions. “Preparing a master plan for a new city from scratch is relatively easier. Correcting the existing situa-tion in Karachi is a major challenge for consultants and urban planners,” he said, urging them to pro-vide recommendations not only for improving the city’s condition but also for ensuring effective im-plementation of the plan. Recalling his personal association with Karachi, the chief minister said he had witnessed the city’s rapid expansion. He observed that its growth had been accompanied by serious planning failures, which had made subsequent efforts to improve urban infrastructure increasingly difficult. Referring to the 2020 monsoon flooding in Yousuf Goth, District West, he said roads that had originally been designed with proper carriageways, central islands and storm-water drains had subsequently been encroached upon. Shops had been established on service roads, medians and drainage channels, undermining the original infrastructure. He acknowledged that successive governments, including his own, had made mistakes that contribut-ed to the city’s present condition. “Once a city develops structural problems, correcting them becomes extremely difficult,” he said, add-ing that the government could not resolve urban challenges without the cooperation of residents, planners, builders, utility companies and other stakeholders. Murad Ali Shah cited Sukkur as an example of how sustained investment could improve urban infra-structure. He said the city’s roads and drainage system had been improved over the past seven to eight years, including through public-private partnerships. Highlighting delays caused by utility companies, he recalled that during construction of the Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Expressway, the relocation of K-Electric infrastructure had delayed work despite payment for shifting its lines. He said utility companies and even the Water and Sewerage Board often took considerable time to relocate their networks. The chief minister said the absence of accurate maps of underground water, sewerage and electricity lines had also complicated development projects. The provincial government had undertaken GIS sur-veys to map underground utilities to a considerable extent, he added. He stressed that traffic management and parking requirements must be incorporated into urban de-velopment plans. Allocating commercial shops on land reserved for parking, he warned, further aggravated congestion and undermined the functioning of cities. The chief minister said the government had arranged funds for Karachi’s development despite the difficulties associated with undertaking construction work in a city with a population of around 25 mil-lion. He also referred to vision of Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari to transform Kara-chi into a modern, smart city meeting international standards. The objective, he said, was to make the metropolis economically stronger and more attractive for business and tourism. The CM said urban development should ultimately improve the everyday lives of citizens. The gov-ernment was pursuing projects relating to roads, highways, bridges, public transport, parks, healthcare, education, water supply and drainage across the province. He also cited the Sindh Peoples Housing Scheme, inter-district roads, improvements to the irrigation network, hospital and educational infrastructure, industrial development, sports facilities, market re-habilitation, plantation drives and major water and sanitation schemes as part of the provincial devel-opment agenda. The chief minister said the objective was to develop cities where all citizens could enjoy equal oppor-tunities for progress, better services, security and a sustainable future. He expressed appreciation for the collaboration between the Sindh Master Planning Authority, NED University and UN-Habitat, saying collective efforts were essential to making Sindh’s cities more livea-ble, resilient and economically productive Earlier, the minister for local government, housing and town planning Syed Nasir Shah said the de-partment had been entrusted with the responsibility of urban planning in Sindh and had established the Sindh Master Planning Authority to oversee city planning, development control and sustainable urban growth. He said master planning provided a long-term framework for determining the location and develop-ment of residential and commercial areas, industries, roads, public transport, parks, hospitals, educa-tional institutions and essential municipal services. He said the Sindh Cities Forum would provide an important platform for government institutions, uni-versities, urban planners, experts and other stakeholders to exchange ideas and develop practical so-lutions for the province’s growing cities. Both speakers emphasised that sustainable urban development required coordinated planning, public participation, efficient use of available resources and stronger cooperation between government de-partments, academic institutions, local authorities and the private sector.

Addressing the Sindh Cities Forum 2026, organised by Sindh Master Planning Authority (SMPA) in col-laboration with NED University and UN-Habitat to mark World Cities Day at Golf Club’s Convention Centre, the chief minister said master planning was essential to address the growing challenges of ur-banisation, including unplanned construction, traffic congestion, water shortages, inadequate drainage and the effects of climate change. According to the minister for local government, housing and town planning, master plans for 17 cities had been completed, while work on the remaining 14 was in its final stages. The government had so far issued notification for the master plans of nine cities: Sukkur, Larkana, Mirpurkhas, Umerkot, Mithi, Islamkot, Dadu, Nawabshah and Naushahro Feroze.
The CM said work on the master plans for Karachi and Hyderabad was progressing rapidly. Internation-al consultants had been engaged for Karachi’s master plan, which, he acknowledged, would be a par-ticularly challenging exercise given the city’s existing urban conditions.
“Preparing a master plan for a new city from scratch is relatively easier. Correcting the existing situa-tion in Karachi is a major challenge for consultants and urban planners,” he said, urging them to pro-vide recommendations not only for improving the city’s condition but also for ensuring effective im-plementation of the plan. Recalling his personal association with Karachi, the chief minister said he had witnessed the city’s rapid expansion. He observed that its growth had been accompanied by serious planning failures, which had made subsequent efforts to improve urban infrastructure increasingly difficult.
Referring to the 2020 monsoon flooding in Yousuf Goth, District West, he said roads that had originally been designed with proper carriageways, central islands and storm-water drains had subsequently been encroached upon. Shops had been established on service roads, medians and drainage channels, undermining the original infrastructure.
He acknowledged that successive governments, including his own, had made mistakes that contribut-ed to the city’s present condition. “Once a city develops structural problems, correcting them becomes extremely difficult,” he said, add-ing that the government could not resolve urban challenges without the cooperation of residents, planners, builders, utility companies and other stakeholders. Murad Ali Shah cited Sukkur as an example of how sustained investment could improve urban infra-structure. He said the city’s roads and drainage system had been improved over the past seven to eight years, including through public-private partnerships.
Highlighting delays caused by utility companies, he recalled that during construction of the Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Expressway, the relocation of K-Electric infrastructure had delayed work despite payment for shifting its lines. He said utility companies and even the Water and Sewerage Board often took considerable time to relocate their networks.
The chief minister said the absence of accurate maps of underground water, sewerage and electricity lines had also complicated development projects. The provincial government had undertaken GIS sur-veys to map underground utilities to a considerable extent, he added.
He stressed that traffic management and parking requirements must be incorporated into urban de-velopment plans. 
Allocating commercial shops on land reserved for parking, he warned, further aggravated congestion and undermined the functioning of cities.
The chief minister said the government had arranged funds for Karachi’s development despite the difficulties associated with undertaking construction work in a city with a population of around 25 mil-lion.
He also referred to vision of Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari to transform Kara-chi into a modern, smart city meeting international standards. The objective, he said, was to make the metropolis economically stronger and more attractive for business and tourism.
The CM said urban development should ultimately improve the everyday lives of citizens. The gov-ernment was pursuing projects relating to roads, highways, bridges, public transport, parks, healthcare, education, water supply and drainage across the province.
He also cited the Sindh Peoples Housing Scheme, inter-district roads, improvements to the irrigation network, hospital and educational infrastructure, industrial development, sports facilities, market re-habilitation, plantation drives and major water and sanitation schemes as part of the provincial devel-opment agenda. 
The chief minister said the objective was to develop cities where all citizens could enjoy equal oppor-tunities for progress, better services, security and a sustainable future.
He expressed appreciation for the collaboration between the Sindh Master Planning Authority, NED University and UN-Habitat, saying collective efforts were essential to making Sindh’s cities more livea-ble, resilient and economically productive
Earlier, the minister for local government, housing and town planning Syed Nasir Shah said the de-partment had been entrusted with the responsibility of urban planning in Sindh and had established the Sindh Master Planning Authority to oversee city planning, development control and sustainable urban growth.
He said master planning provided a long-term framework for determining the location and develop-ment of residential and commercial areas, industries, roads, public transport, parks, hospitals, educa-tional institutions and essential municipal services.
He said the Sindh Cities Forum would provide an important platform for government institutions, uni-versities, urban planners, experts and other stakeholders to exchange ideas and develop practical so-lutions for the province’s growing cities.
Both speakers emphasised that sustainable urban development required coordinated planning, public participation, efficient use of available resources and stronger cooperation between government de-partments, academic institutions, local authorities and the private sector.

headline: Cricket Centre Club edge Khizra Club in last-ball thriller
description: LAHORE (Staff Reporter): Cricket Centre Club pulled off a thrilling one-wicket victory over Khizra Club on the final delivery in an exciting 35-over Festival
author: The Nation
article_text: LAHORE (Staff Reporter): Cricket Centre Club pulled off a thrilling one-wicket victory over Khizra Club on the final delivery in an exciting 35-over Festival Match at Cricket Centre, Model Town. Batting first, Khizra Club posted an impressive 255-4 in their allotted 35 overs. Hasan Mudassir top-scored with 65, while Saad Khan (60), Mohsin Ali (50) and Rana Arsalan (37) also made valuable contributions. Hasnain claimed two wickets for Cricket Centre Club.In reply, Cricket Centre Club chased down the target on the last ball, finishing at 256-9. Ali Zafar led the successful pursuit with an unbeaten 68, while Usman scored 42 and Inaam contributed 26. For Khizra Club, Ahmed Iqbal took three wickets, while Jaish Ali and Muaz Awan claimed two apiece. Ali Zafar, Hasan Mudassir and Ahmed Iqbal received cash awards of Rs5,000 each from Khizra Club patron Riaz Ahmed for their outstanding performances. Cantonment Zone Cricket Association President Mashhood Hussain Shirazi attended as chief guest and appreciated both teams’ performances and sportsmanship. Khizra Cricket Club Chairman Abid Hussain also highlighted the importance of club cricket in developing young talent and promoting a positive sporting culture. Riazuddin and Rab Nawaz performed umpiring duties, while Ziauddin was the scorer.

headline: Memorial Girls Basketball Series begins today
description: LAHORE - The inaugural Berger Paints Trophy Najam Sheikh Memorial Girls Basketball Triangular Series will begin on Sunday at Ayub Khuhro Complex, Larkana,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The inaugural Berger Paints Trophy Najam Sheikh Memorial Girls Basketball Triangular Series will begin on Sunday at Ayub Khuhro Complex, Larkana, featuring teams from Karachi, Sukkur and the host city. The opening match will see Larkana take on Sukkur at 10am, followed by Karachi’s clash with Larkana at noon. Larkana Deputy Commissioner Tariq Manzoor Chandio will attend as chief guest and distribute prizes.

description: LAHORE - LAHORE: Aitchison College clinched the title of the 56th Jaffer Memorial Inter-School Hockey Championship 2026 after defeating Govt Quaid-e-Azam Lab
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - LAHORE: Aitchison College clinched the title of the 56th Jaffer Memorial Inter-School Hockey Championship 2026 after defeating Govt Quaid-e-Azam Lab Model High School, Sargodha, 3-0 in the final at Aitchison College Lahore. Rana Samiullah opened the scoring in the second minute of the first quarter, while Shahidullah doubled the lead in the 10th minute. Rana Samiullah completed the victory with his second goal in the fifth minute of the second quarter. In the third-place match, DPS Lahore defeated Govt High School Dhing Shah, Kasur, 4-2. Bilal scored twice, while Nauman and Usman added one goal each. M Asghar and Nadeem scored for Kasur. Former PHF president and Olympian Qasim Zia was the chief guest. Abdul Rehman QLS received the best goalkeeper award, while Aitchison’s Aryan the best player.

headline: Brotherly Pak-Saudi ties offer vast opportunities for economic coop: Jam Kamal
description: ISLAMABAD - The newly appointed Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Albugamy Saturday called on Federal Minister for Commerce Jam
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The newly appointed Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Albugamy Saturday called on Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan to discuss strengthening bilateral trade, economic cooperation and investment opportunities between the two brotherly countries.

Welcoming the ambassador, Jam Kamal Khan reaffirmed Pakistan’s deep-rooted and historic relations with Saudi Arabia, highlighting the Kingdom’s special significance as the custodian of the Haram. He said the government of Pakistan had made sustained efforts over the past three years to further strengthen bilateral relations through enhanced government-to-government, business-to-business and people-to-people engagement.

The commerce minister emphasized that the longstanding brotherly relationship offered considerable opportunities for greater economic integration, particularly in view of Saudi Arabia’s economic diversification under Vision 2030 and Pakistan’s production and industrial capabilities.

He highlighted the potential for cooperation in scaling up production, improving product quality, adopting modern technologies and strengthening industrial competitiveness. He noted that collaboration in these areas could enable Pakistani businesses to better meet the requirements of the Saudi market while creating mutually beneficial economic opportunities.

The minister also underscored the importance of expanding Pakistan’s export base and strengthening private-sector partnerships to translate the growing economic engagement into tangible trade outcomes.

During the meeting, the Saudi ambassador reaffirmed the enduring bonds of brotherhood between the two countries and assured continued support for strengthening bilateral economic relations. He highlighted opportunities for enhanced regional connectivity and cooperation, particularly in the agriculture sector.

Both sides also discussed the Pakistan–Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Free Trade Agreement and its early signing and implementation. The minister noted that the agreement would provide an important opportunity to enhance market access, expand bilateral trade and strengthen economic engagement.

The Saudi ambassador expressed his commitment to maintaining close engagement with the ministry of commerce to facilitate greater economic cooperation and identify new avenues for mutually beneficial partnerships.

Both sides agreed to maintain regular coordination and follow-up engagement to advance bilateral trade, investment and agricultural cooperation, with a shared objective of translating their longstanding friendship into stronger economic ties.

headline: FG/Din/Sheikhoo edge DP to reach Memorial Polo final
description: LAHORE - FG/Din/Sheikhoo booked their place in the main final of the 14th Maj Gen Saeed-uz-Zaman Memorial Polo Cup 2026, sponsored by JS Bank, after edging out
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - FG/Din/Sheikhoo booked their place in the main final of the 14th Maj Gen Saeed-uz-Zaman Memorial Polo Cup 2026, sponsored by JS Bank, after edging out Diamond Paints/Platinum Homes 6-5 in a thrilling sudden-death semifinal at Lahore Garrison Polo Grounds on Saturday. The closely contested encounter went down to the wire, with FG/Din/Sheikhoo eventually securing victory in the fifth chukker of extra time to seal their place in the title showdown. Hamza Mawaz Khan led the winning side with an outstanding hat-trick, while Sheikh Muhammad Raffay contributed two goals and Mian Abbas Mukhtar added one. For Diamond Paints/Platinum Homes, Mir Huzaifa Ahmed scored three goals, while Saqib Khan Khakwani struck twice. Meanwhile, Master Paints/Rijas captured the subsidiary final after overcoming FG/Din/SQ 5-4 in another exciting encounter. Raja Mikayial Sami was the star performer for Master Paints/Rijas, scoring a superb hat-trick, while Saim Abbas and Sufi Muhammad Haroon contributed one goal apiece. For FG/Din/SQ, Abbas Mukhtar, Farhad Sheikh, Amin Fazal and Ayan Salman scored one goal each. The tournament’s main final will be played on Sunday at Fortress Stadium, where Diamond Paints/Imperial will take on FG/Din/Sheikhoo for the prestigious trophy. Begum Saeed-uz-Zaman Janjua will grace the final as the chief guest.

headline: Abid Iqbal maintains lead at 43rd Millat Tractors Governors Cup
description: LAHORE - Young golfer Abid Iqbal tightened his grip on the leaderboard with an impressive seven-under-par net score of 137 after two rounds of the 43rd Millat
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Young golfer Abid Iqbal tightened his grip on the leaderboard with an impressive seven-under-par net score of 137 after two rounds of the 43rd Millat Tractors Governors Cup, putting himself in a strong position to claim the prestigious title ahead of Sunday’s final round. The 23-year-old has been in outstanding form, displaying consistency, confidence and excellent shot-making to establish a significant advantage over his nearest challengers in the competition. Qasim Ali Khan stands second with a net score of 142, five strokes behind the leader, while Ahmed Zafar occupies third position with 150. Mohsin Zafar is further back in fourth place with 152, as the battle for the remaining top positions continues. Son of a senior golf professional, Abid has developed his golfing abilities through dedication, disciplined practice and a solid understanding of the game’s fundamentals. His powerful long hitting, accurate execution and composed approach have distinguished him from a competitive field featuring several accomplished golfers. His performance across the opening two rounds has underlined his growing maturity and ability to deliver under competitive pressure. However, with one round remaining, the young leader will need to maintain his concentration and consistency to convert his impressive advantage into championship glory. Qasim Ali Khan and the other leading contenders will be eager to mount a strong challenge, making Sunday’s final round particularly important. With a five-stroke cushion over his closest rival, Abid has given himself an excellent opportunity to finish on top. Nevertheless, golf’s unpredictable nature leaves room for a final-day contest, where composure, precision and sound course management could determine the ultimate winner.

Qasim Ali Khan stands second with a net score of 142, five strokes behind the leader, while Ahmed Zafar occupies third position with 150. Mohsin Zafar is further back in fourth place with 152, as the battle for the remaining top positions continues. Son of a senior golf professional, Abid has developed his golfing abilities through dedication, disciplined practice and a solid understanding of the game’s fundamentals. His powerful long hitting, accurate execution and composed approach have distinguished him from a competitive field featuring several accomplished golfers.
His performance across the opening two rounds has underlined his growing maturity and ability to deliver under competitive pressure. However, with one round remaining, the young leader will need to maintain his concentration and consistency to convert his impressive advantage into championship glory.  Qasim Ali Khan and the other leading contenders will be eager to mount a strong challenge, making Sunday’s final round particularly important. With a five-stroke cushion over his closest rival, Abid has given himself an excellent opportunity to finish on top. Nevertheless, golf’s unpredictable nature leaves room for a final-day contest, where composure, precision and sound course management could determine the ultimate winner.

headline: WB okays $150m programme to boost municipal revenues, services in Sindh
description: ISLAMABAD - The World Bank Group’s Board of Executive Directors has approved $150 million in financing for a programme aimed at improving urban property
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The World Bank Group’s Board of Executive Directors has approved $150 million in financing for a programme aimed at improving urban property tax collection and strengthening municipal service delivery in Sindh, particularly Karachi.

The Sindh Property Revenues Enhancement Program (Sindh PREP) would support the provincial government in improving urban immovable property tax (UIPT) collection and strengthening the service delivery capacity of selected local councils, a WB news release said on Saturday. “Cities that can raise their own revenues can plan and invest for the long term,” World Bank Country Director for Pakistan Bolormaa Amgaabazar said. She said Sindh’s local councils currently depended on provincial transfers for more than 95 per cent of their revenues.

By helping Karachi collect property taxes from residents and businesses and reinvesting most of the revenue in local services, the country director said, the programme would enable cities to finance the infrastructure they needed.

Despite being one of the world’s largest cities, Karachi currently collects only around $8.5 million annually in property taxes, while cities of comparable size collect 82 to 350 times more.

The programme aims to increase Karachi’s annual property tax collection to $85 million by raising compliance from 20 to 50 per cent. It would strengthen tax collection, compliance and administration through a property tax management information system covering billing, payment processing and grievance redress, alongside integrated financial management information systems across local councils.

About 70 per cent of the collected property tax revenue will be reinvested directly in municipal infrastructure and services in participating local councils. The programme would benefit Karachi’s 25 local councils, covering 3.58 million people.

Its performance-based financing mechanism would link funding to annual assessments conducted by an Independent Verification Agent, with the resulting allocations used to rehabilitate climate-resilient municipal infrastructure and improve services. The investments would cover drainage, sewerage, schools, fire stations, roads and street lighting. The programme also includes a $40 million Investment Project Financing component to expand property surveys and property tax administration to 20 local councils in other urban centres of Sindh, indirectly benefiting around 4.5 million people.

“Karachi has significant untapped potential to generate revenues from its property base and use those resources to fund the infrastructure its residents and businesses need,” said Davison Muchadenyika, Senior Urban Development Specialist at the World Bank.

He said the programme would help Sindh strengthen fiscal sustainability, enabling cities to plan, invest and deliver services effectively through their own resources.

headline: Sensational South Africa seal the Test series in Capetown
description: CAPE TOWN - Simon Harmer produced a sensational bowling performance to guide South Africa to a commanding 176-run victory over Australia in the third and final
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: CAPE TOWN - Simon Harmer produced a sensational bowling performance to guide South Africa to a commanding 176-run victory over Australia in the third and final Test at Newlands on Saturday, securing a memorable 2-1 series triumph. Chasing a challenging 288-run target for victory, Australia crumbled to 111 all out in 57.1 overs on the fifth day, surrendering the series after winning the opening Test. South Africa bounced back emphatically, winning the second Test by an innings before completing the decisive victory in Cape Town. Fast bowler Kagiso Rabada set the tone for South Africa with a devastating opening spell, removing Matt Renshaw and Marnus Labuschagne in the first over to leave Australia reeling at five for two. Rabada struck again to dismiss Travis Head, while a run-out further compounded the visitors’ difficulties. Harmer then took control of the contest, dismantling Australia’s middle and lower order with remarkable precision. The experienced off-spinner claimed six wickets for just 16 runs in 21.1 overs, completing a match-winning 10-wicket haul and earning the Player of the Match award. Cameron Green offered some resistance with a patient 27 off 110 balls, including three boundaries, but Harmer eventually ended his innings to reduce Australia to 62 for eight. Pat Cummins contributed 11 before becoming Harmer’s fifth victim, while Josh Hazlewood was bowled for a duck to complete the South African victory. Nathan Lyon remained unbeaten on 33 from 57 deliveries, striking six fours, and shared a stubborn 45-run partnership with Cummins that briefly delayed the inevitable. Rabada provided excellent support to Harmer, finishing with three wickets for 39 runs in 14 overs.

headline: Top-up Fakhar Zaman leads Pakistan’s record chase to ODI tri-series glory
description: LAHORE - Fakhar Zaman delivered when it mattered most, ending a nearly three-year wait for an ODI century with a commanding 127 as Pakistan defeated Sri Lanka
author: Azhar Khan
article_text: LAHORE - Fakhar Zaman delivered when it mattered most, ending a nearly three-year wait for an ODI century with a commanding 127 as Pakistan defeated Sri Lanka by three wickets to lift the home tri-series trophy at Gaddafi Stadium on Saturday. Chasing 326, Pakistan reached 329-7 in 48.3 overs, completing a successful pursuit with nine balls to spare. The victory was built around Fakhar’s 99-ball innings, which featured 11 fours and six sixes and brought his 12th ODI hundred. Pakistan’s reply began badly as Dilshan Madushanka removed Maaz Sadaqat and Babar Azam in successive overs, leaving the hosts 14 for two. Fakhar steadied the innings alongside young wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig, and their third-wicket stand of 149 transformed the chase. Baig struck 74 from 75 balls, including 11 boundaries, before Maheesh Theekshana ended the partnership. Fakhar then added 57 with Salman Ali Agha, reaching three figures before Madushanka bowled him for 127 in the 34th over. Agha made 17, but Pakistan still needed a substantial contribution from the lower order. Hasan Nawaz and Arafat Minhas answered the call with a decisive 94-run partnership. Minhas made a rapid 61 from 31 balls, hitting four sixes and three fours, while Nawaz provided support. Asitha Fernando dismissed Minhas and Faheem Ashraf in the 48th over to revive Sri Lanka’s hopes, but captain Shaheen Shah Afridi settled the contest by launching Madushanka for a six to bring up the winning runs. Earlier, Sri Lanka posted 325-8 after being sent in. Kamindu Mendis led their innings with a superb 131 from 128 deliveries, including 12 fours and two sixes. He shared a 146-run third-wicket partnership with Pavan Rathnayake, who scored 77 off 65 balls. Pakistan captain Shaheen, Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf and Salman Ali Agha claimed two wickets apiece, keeping Sri Lanka from pushing beyond 325. Fakhar’s hundred was his first in 15 ODI innings, since an unbeaten 126 against New Zealand at the 2023 World Cup. His 4,000-run milestone and record-equalling second century in an ODI tournament final added further significance to a defining performance. The century also matched Saeed Anwar’s mark of two centuries in ODI tournament finals, following Fakhar’s 2017 Champions Trophy final hundred against India at The Oval in London.

headline: PIA resumes direct flights to China
description: BEIJING - Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has resumed its flight operations between Pakistan and China, with the first flight operating on October 30,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
BEIJING - Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has resumed its flight operations between Pakistan and China, with the first flight operating on October 30, reconnecting Islamabad and Beijing through direct air services. The resumption marks a significant milestone in strengthening aviation links between the two friendly countries and reflects PIA’s commitment to restoring and maintaining regular operations in the Chinese market. Under the renewed schedule, PIA will operate weekly flights between Islamabad and Beijing every Friday, providing passengers with a direct and convenient travel option between the two capitals. The airline also aims to offer competitive fares while ensuring consistent and reliable services. In a major step towards expanding its network across China, PIA has strengthened its cooperation with three leading Chinese airlines, including Air China, Shenzhen Airlines and Hainan Airlines. Through its partnership with Air China, passengers will benefit from onward connections to various domestic destinations through Beijing, a major aviation hub. Shenzhen Airlines will facilitate connectivity to key destinations through its Shenzhen-based network and other Chinese gateways, while Hainan Airlines will provide additional travel options through its network, including connections via Haikou.

These strategic partnerships will facilitate passenger connectivity to 26 destinations across China, offering greater travel flexibility and convenience beyond Beijing.

The restored air link is expected to benefit Pakistani and Chinese students, academic communities, business travellers, investors, commercial organizations, families, expatriates and tourists travelling between the two countries.

The improved connectivity is also expected to contribute to the promotion of bilateral trade, tourism, investment, educational cooperation and people-to-people exchanges, further strengthening the longstanding friendship between Pakistan and China.

PIA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening its presence in the Chinese aviation market through reliable services, competitive fares, strategic airline partnerships and regular flight operations.

The national flag carrier will continue working with its Chinese partners and relevant stakeholders to enhance air connectivity and provide passengers with more convenient travel opportunities between the two countries.

The resumption of direct flights and expansion of connecting services represent an important development in promoting closer economic, commercial and people-to-people ties between Pakistan and China.

headline: Pakistan cautiously optimistic on Iran-US peace talks: DG ISPR
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan ‘cautiously optimistic’ about its role in mediating between Iran and the United States, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan ‘cautiously optimistic’ about its role in mediating between Iran and the United States, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, the spokesman for the Pakistan military, stated in an exclusive interview with Reuters published Saturday. Director-General of the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry stated the Chief of Defense Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir visited Tehran twice in October to help end an eight-month war. He stated that Pakistan is “invested in peace inside” the country and the wider world. The military spokesperson stated that the Field Marshal Asim Munir, possessing “that vision and strategy” and the “trust that he enjoys internally and externally”, has played an extremely “critical role” in “making the parties understand and realize that the path of destruction serves no one except those who have to gain something out of that destruction.” He warned that “powerful spoilers” still exist who want the conflict to continue. Pakistan in August became part of a significant regional security arrangement. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Türkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, which establishes that an attack on any member nation constitutes an attack on all signatories, reported by Reuters. When asked if the alliance was open to anyone, DG ISPR stated that any country was welcome to join the pact if it aligned with a shared vision of regional peace. He stated that while Pakistan will defend Saudi Arabia and protect the Islamic holy sites of Makkah and Medina, the country will not participate in military operations in Yemen, according to Reuters. The eight-month conflict between Iran and the United States has destabilized the Middle East and increased global oil prices. In 2026, Pakistan served as the primary diplomatic mediator between the United States and Iran, leveraging its strategic ties to broker a temporary halt to regional hostilities. Pakistan hosted high-level talks that successfully culminated in the signing of the historic Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on June 17, 2026, alongside regional facilitators like Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Qatar, and Egypt. Pakistan has continued its vigorous mediation efforts into late October 2026, utilizing high-stakes diplomatic visits to Tehran and regional platforms to urge both Washington and Tehran to return to the negotiating table. The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was a 14-point interim peace agreement signed on June 17, 2026, by US President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. The deal established a 60-day window for peace talks by trading an immediate ceasefire, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and the release of $300 billion in frozen assets for the IAEA-supervised downblending of Iran’s enriched uranium stockpile. It marked the first direct contractual negotiation between US and Iranian leadership in decades and remains the baseline blueprint for ongoing regional diplomacy.

headline: The silence of PTI in KP and the crisis of leadership
description: ISLAMABAD - The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) failure to articulate a clear political strategy following the imposition of an emergency and
author: Imran Mukhtar
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) failure to articulate a clear political strategy following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa raises a fundamental question: is the party’s muted opposition is a retreat from its known style of politics or a reflection of a deeper leadership crisis? The party of incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan had created much hype for its planned long march on Islamabad till October 11 when the federal government made the PTI-ruled provincial government and the KP Assembly dysfunctional through the imposition of governor’s rule. With the detention of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and other provincial leadership of the party, the protest long march diminished within a few minutes and since then the central leadership could not give a definite political strategy to the party on how to get out of the ongoing crisis. PTI loses ground Following its failed strategy to give a strong response to its opponents, the PTI has lost confidence in the eyes of its workers. The PTI had been building pressure on the federal government through its agitational politics. However, given the central leadership’s lack of response to the October 11 developments, this political leverage appears to have dissipated. The party is facing criticism, both from within its own ranks and outside, for failing to mobilise a sizable number of supporters to protest the removal of its provincial government, despite having governed KP since 2013 and accumulated considerable political capital over three consecutive terms. At one point, the protest long march call of the PTI had forced the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PMLN)-led ruling alliance to initiate the talks process after the latter had an understanding that the opposition party could give it a tough time after reaching Islamabad with a large number of crowd. That leverage, however, no longer appears to be available to the PTI, with little indication that the federal government feels the same pressure to engage. One can give some benefit of doubt to the PTI that perhaps the party’s recent decision to avoid agitation is a retreat from its politics of agitation. However, the party is facing deeper problems that has brought it to the point where it has even lost the limited space that was available to it following last general elections. Leadership Crisis The leadership crisis within the party is visible. Since it lost its government in KP, a blame game is going on within the party with many questioning the role of central leadership including interim Chairman Gohar Ali Khan and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja. There is a revolt-like situation against the leadership. Several members of the PTI insist that the central leaders should quit their positions as they failed to give an effective strategy to the party before and after governor’s rule. The role of the opposition leader in the National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai is also being discussed critically within party circles as many saying that he has failed to fulfill his primary responsibility of engaging with the government. Several party leaders believe that it was the duty of the central leadership to save the KP government from suspension by successfully negotiating with the Centre on counterterrorism operations and winding up the long march at earliest. They say that the central leadership not only failed to understand the sensitivity of the situation but also could not pursue the provincial leadership and hardcore elements to bring some flexibility in their stance. “With the suspension of the KP government, the PTI has lost all protections it previously enjoyed,” a senior party leader commented. He said it was the responsibility of the central leadership to guide the younger and inexperienced members of the party, including Chief Minister Afridi, to prevent the situation that had now emerged.

headline: Syria considering joining Makkah alliance, says FM
description: MANAMA - Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Al-Shaibani said Saturday that Damascus is evaluating the possibility of joining the Makkah alliance, a regional
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: MANAMA - Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Al-Shaibani said Saturday that Damascus is evaluating the possibility of joining the Makkah alliance, a regional pact bringing together Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan. “Discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria’s entry into the Makkah alliance,” Al-Shaibani said during a session on regional security at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA). The foreign minister described Syria as an integral part of regional security and reaffirmed Damascus’ support for initiatives aimed at strengthening regional stability. He stressed that the region was “in greater need than ever” of developing joint deterrence and defense systems to address growing security challenges. Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Al-Shaibani reaffirmed Syria’s support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability throughout the country. He also called on all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states. Separately, Al-Shaibani accused Israel of carrying out more than 1,000 attacks on Syrian territory in less than two years, killing dozens of people. “Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens,” he said. “How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?” he asked. Condemning the attacks, the Syrian foreign minister called for a return to the lines that existed before Dec. 8, 2024, and full implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement between Syria and Israel. He reaffirmed that the Golan Heights is Syrian territory and cited UN Security Council Resolution 497 as the relevant international reference. Following the fall of the Assad regime on Dec. 8, 2024, Israel occupied the Syrian buffer zone established under the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and established military positions inside and outside the zone. The United Nations has described Israel’s presence in the buffer zone as a violation of the agreement.
