cleaned_blocks.text: Tharparkar suffers from repeated droughts. The desert needs a long-term plan focused on water security, resilient livelihoods, healthcare and education, rather than emergency assistance each time the monsoon fails.

In south-eastern Sindh, rain is the basis of life. It determines whether crops grow, livestock survive and families can sustain themselves. When the monsoon fails, the consequences extend beyond farming to drinking water, food security, children’s education, and physical and mental health. Each drought brings the same challenges: water shortages, loss of grazing land and livestock, and migration. Why does a region repeatedly facing drought still lack a comprehensive plan to protect its people before the next crisis?

Tharparkar has experienced severe dry periods in the 1960s, 1980s, late 1990s and early 2000s, followed by a prolonged crisis from 2013 to 2018. Covering 19,638 square kilometres and home to approximately 1.78 million people, according to the 2023 census, its scattered settlements and limited water resources make public service delivery difficult. Its dependence on rainfall leaves communities particularly vulnerable.

Agriculture and livestock remain central to local livelihoods. Farmers depend on monsoon rains to grow millet, guar and sesame, while grazing lands sustain goats, sheep, cattle and other animals. Insufficient rainfall damages crops, depletes grazing fields and increases fodder costs. Livestock represent more than income; they are a family’s financial security during difficult times. Distress sales and depleted savings undermine recovery and deepen vulnerability.

Migration to irrigated areas of Sindh in search of fodder, grazing land and temporary employment has long been a coping mechanism. However, displacement comes at a social cost. Children miss school, families lose access to essential services, and women, older people and persons with disabilities face additional barriers to healthcare and clean water.

Water scarcity remains a fundamental development challenge. Communities rely on rainwater, groundwater, wells and local tanks, many of which become unreliable during prolonged dry periods. In some areas, groundwater is either too deep or unsuitable for drinking.

Drought also disrupts education and healthcare. Financial hardship and migration force children to miss lessons or leave school altogether. School retention programmes, targeted household assistance and continuity arrangements for mobile families must be strengthened, alongside nutrition and social protection services.

Remote villages often lack adequate healthcare facilities and staff. Poor roads, muddy tracks and limited emergency transport delay referrals, particularly for pregnant women, children and seriously ill patients. Investment in rural health facilities, staff recruitment and retention, four-wheel-drive ambulances, all-weather roads and mobile health teams is essential.

The psychological toll of drought also demands attention. Debt, crop failure, livestock losses and uncertainty heighten distress. Media reports recorded 122 deaths by suicide in Tharparkar between January and September 2026. While suicide cannot be attributed to drought alone, vulnerable communities need accessible counselling, trained frontline health workers, referral services and public awareness initiatives to reduce stigma. Mental healthcare must become part of primary healthcare rather than an emergency afterthought.

The government of Sindh needs to replace reactive relief with a coordinated programme that reduces the impact of drought before household resources are exhausted. A district-level early-warning system should integrate rainfall forecasts, vegetation conditions, groundwater data, crop assessments and livestock health reports. Clear thresholds must trigger timely assistance, including food support, fodder, veterinary care and emergency water supplies.

Livestock protection should remain central to drought preparedness. Community fodder banks, vaccination campaigns, mobile veterinary teams and accessible animal health services can prevent losses. Assistance must be sufficient to prevent distress sales and protect breeding animals.

Livelihood diversification is equally important. Support for enterprises, women-led businesses, drought-resilient agriculture, livestock value chains, vocational training and local employment can reduce dependence on a single rainy season. Tharparkar’s mineral resources and cultural heritage offer opportunities, but development must generate meaningful employment and benefits for surrounding communities.

Social protection must also integrate education, nutrition and healthcare, ensuring children remain in school, pregnant women access essential services and temporary economic shocks do not become long-term deprivation.

munities and technical experts, and determine whether a dedicated authority would improve coordination, accountability and implementation.

If established, it must have a clear legal mandate, defined responsibilities, transparent budgeting and measurable targets. Its work should integrate water management, livestock development, climate-resilient agriculture, healthcare, education, infrastructure and livelihood diversification. headline: Beyond Seasonal Smog
description: Pakistan’s winter smog is not an unavoidable seasonal affliction; it reflects pollution that policy has failed to prevent. As per reports, between
author: The Nation
article_text:
Pakistan’s winter smog is not an unavoidable seasonal affliction; it reflects pollution that policy has failed to prevent. As per reports, between October 1 and 29, 13,241 fire spots were detected in Punjab, 4.2 times the 3,158 recorded in Indian Punjab. Around 92 per cent of detections in Pakistan’s Punjab were on farmland and likely linked to crop-residue burning. Detected crop fires fell by 95pc in Indian Punjab between 2021 and 2025, while Pakistan’s count rose by 33pc between 2019 and 2025.

Crop burning is not the only source of smog. Industrial and vehicle emissions, brick kilns, waste burning, and construction dust also contribute. Fires across the rice-growing belt around Lahore add a seasonal burden when stagnant conditions trap pollutants close to the ground. The consequences extend beyond poor visibility: prolonged exposure aggravates respiratory and cardiovascular illnesses, disrupts schooling and work, and strains healthcare services. Children, older people, and those with existing illnesses are especially vulnerable.

Climate change compounds the problem. Rising temperatures and erratic rainfall pressure water supplies and agricultural cycles; heat and dry conditions can heighten fire risks. Pollution adds to the climate burden, leaving communities less resilient to extreme weather. Temporary measures and visible displays of enforcement are too little, too late while pollution sources remain intact. Anti-smog guns, sporadic inspections and short-lived crackdowns cannot replace prevention or changes in crop-residue and waste management.

A lasting response requires affordable machinery and incentives to help farmers manage residue without burning, reliable public data, consistent enforcement, cleaner industry and transport, and adequately resourced local monitoring. Air quality must be treated as a year-round concern, not a seasonal emergency.

headline: LPG Policy
description: Pakistan’s proposed changes to the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market have prompted a necessary review, with the Prime Minister constituting a
author: The Nation
article_text:
Pakistan’s proposed changes to the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market have prompted a necessary review, with the Prime Minister constituting a ministerial committee to examine the Petroleum Division’s proposed reforms. The plan would transfer import and price-setting responsibilities from the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) to state-owned enterprises, introducing import-parity pricing linked to Saudi Aramco rates and actual import costs. The review comes amid a widening gap between official and market prices, raising questions about how reforms will affect consumers.

For households reliant on LPG, pricing is not an abstract matter of market regulation. It is a basic cost of living. With an 11.57kg cylinder reportedly selling for Rs6,000 to Rs7,200 against Ogra’s notified price of Rs3,296, the burden is already considerable. Families without access to piped natural gas, particularly in rural areas and smaller towns, have little choice but to absorb these increases or compromise on essential domestic needs. Any policy that overlooks this reality risks making an already expensive source of household energy even less accessible.

The proposed involvement of state-owned enterprises may offer greater purchasing capacity and oversight, but changing the institution responsible for pricing does not, by itself, guarantee affordability. Import costs, transportation, market margins, and supply disruptions must all be accounted for transparently. Equally, the concerns raised by private-sector stakeholders regarding competition and the proposed pricing mechanism deserve careful examination. A market with limited competition can leave consumers exposed to arbitrary price movements.

The committee’s review must therefore produce more than an administrative restructuring. Pakistan needs a pricing framework that reflects genuine supply costs while preventing excessive margins, hoarding and profiteering. Regular market monitoring, transparent price disclosures, effective competition oversight and targeted assistance for low-income households must form its foundation.

headline: The Global Cost
description: The possibility of US President Donald Trump authorising a major military offensive against Iran following potential Republican setbacks in the November
author: The Nation
article_text:
The possibility of US President Donald Trump authorising a major military offensive against Iran following potential Republican setbacks in the November midterm elections raises troubling questions about the direction of an already volatile conflict. A report suggests that electoral repercussions could influence the administration’s calculations, even as diplomatic efforts, facilitated by Qatar, seek to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran. The prospect of renewed military action at such a juncture risks deepening instability far beyond the Middle East.

The conflict has already placed considerable pressure on global energy markets, trade routes and economic stability, with tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz threatening the movement of vital oil supplies. Another round of attacks could drive energy prices higher, intensify inflationary pressures and further burden economies already struggling with the financial consequences of prolonged geopolitical crises.

When a superpower adopts an unpredictable posture towards military intervention, the consequences can extend well beyond its immediate strategic calculations. Retaliatory action, attacks on regional infrastructure and the involvement of other states could transform an already fragile situation into a much broader confrontation. Military strength does not insulate a country from the political, economic and diplomatic backlash of decisions taken without sufficient consideration of their wider implications.

The immediate priority must be to prevent another escalation. Washington and Tehran must give diplomatic channels the opportunity to produce tangible progress, with regional powers supporting efforts to reduce tensions. Domestic political considerations cannot be allowed to dictate decisions carrying consequences for millions beyond national borders. A conflict already exacting a heavy economic and human toll does not need another military chapter. Restraint from the world’s most powerful states is not a concession; it is a responsibility commensurate with the influence they wield.

headline: Development projects to begin soon in Malakand: Commissioner
description: Swat - Commissioner Malakand Division Iqbal Hussain has said that work on several development projects across the division, including Swat,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Swat - Commissioner Malakand Division Iqbal Hussain has said that work on several development projects across the division, including Swat, will begin soon, with urban infrastructure improvement, sewerage system development and city beautification among the administration’s key priorities.

Speaking to a delegation of journalists at his office, the commissioner said a comprehensive plan was being prepared to improve Swat’s urban infrastructure and enhance the city’s natural beauty.

He said the preparation of digital maps would serve as a foundation for planning and implementing various development initiatives.

He added that the proposed projects would focus on improving the sewerage system, upgrading urban facilities and making the city more attractive while preserving its natural beauty.

Commissioner stressed that all government departments must perform their responsibilities in accordance with the principles of merit, transparency and public interest, ensuring better service delivery and addressing public concerns.

He said effective coordination among relevant departments was essential for timely implementation of development projects and ensuring that their benefits reached the public.The delegation was led by Swat Press Club Chairman Fazal Rahim Khan and Swat Union of Journalists President Shahzad Alam. Essa Khankhel, Obaidullah Abid and Haroon Siraj were also present.

headline: Dist admin reviews arrangements for polio booster campaign
description: Peshawar - The district administration on Saturday stepped up monitoring of the ongoing polio booster campaign, with administrative officers
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Peshawar - The district administration on Saturday stepped up monitoring of the ongoing polio booster campaign, with administrative officers visiting different parts of the city to assess field activities and vaccination arrangements. On the directives of Deputy Commissioner Afaq Wazir, the officers visited various localities, interacted with polio teams and monitored the administration of vaccine drops to children.

They reviewed the performance of vaccination staff and met parents to highlight the importance of immunising children against polio, urging them to cooperate with the teams during the campaign. DC Afaq Wazir directed the relevant officials and vaccination teams to ensure that no child under five years of age was missed during the campaign.

headline: AC injured in firing on vehicle in Nowshera
description: NOWSHERA - Assistant Commissioner Oghi, Mansehra, Adil Waseem sustained injuries when unidentified armed men opened fire on his vehicle in Nowshera
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
NOWSHERA - Assistant Commissioner Oghi, Mansehra, Adil Waseem sustained injuries when unidentified armed men opened fire on his vehicle in Nowshera on Saturday. According to police, Adil Waseem was visiting his native village Saleh Khana here. The attackers targeted his vehicle when he was returning from the village. He sustained injuries in the attack and rescuers shifted him to a hospital in Peshawar for medical treatment.

The motive behind the attack and the identity of the assailants were not immediately known.

headline: PESCO disconnects 351 transformers across KP over outstanding dues
description: Peshawar - Peshawar Electric Supply Company (PESCO) has disconnected 351 high loss transformers across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa until outstanding dues
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Peshawar - Peshawar Electric Supply Company (PESCO) has disconnected 351 high loss transformers across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa until outstanding dues are cleared.

According to a press release issued by PESCO Chief Akhtar Hameed Khan, the crackdown will continue until financial losses are recovered.

A circle wise breakdown shows that Khyber Circle recorded highest disconnections with 116 transformers cut off over Rs 117 million in arrears, followed by Swat Circle with 94 transformers disconnected over Rs 100 million.

Additionally, Bannu Circle saw 41 transformers cut off due to Rs40 million in unpaid bills, while Peshawar Circle had 8 transformers disconnected over Rs22.5 million in defaults.

In Buner, PESCO disconnected 39 industrial and 5 domestic transformers, while 43 transformers in Shangla and 5 in Dir were disconnected for unpaid dues and electricity theft.

In D I Khan Circle, 6 transformers were cut off in a single day.

To resolve the issue, PESCO officials are holding negotiations with affected consumers through Khuli Kachehris (open public forums).

Electricity supply is being restored promptly for consumers who settle the outstanding dues for their respective transformers, the statement said.

headline: Anti-encroachment drive continues in Kohat
description: KOHAT - Kohat administration has continued its grand anti-encroachment operation, aimed at restoring public spaces and improving traffic flow in
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
KOHAT - Kohat administration has continued its grand anti-encroachment operation, aimed at restoring public spaces and improving traffic flow in the city, on the directions of Deputy Commissioner (DC) Muhammad Nawaz Wazir.

Assistant Commissioner Naveed Ahmad is supervising the ongoing operation, under which both temporary and permanent encroachments along roadsides are being removed. The drive is intended to clear roads and public passageways, facilitate smooth traffic movement, and ensure easier access for citizens.

According to the district administration, actions against illegal occupations of public land and roads are being carried out in coordination with relevant departments. Citizens have also been urged to refrain from establishing encroachments on government land and public roads and to cooperate with the administration in maintaining public spaces.

Meanwhile, members of the Alizai Welfare Committee called on Deputy Commissioner Muhammad Nawaz Wazir and discussed various public issues, particularly the removal of encroachments and the restoration of government and public access routes in the area.

The delegation appreciated the district administration’s ongoing anti-encroachment campaign and urged authorities to extend the operation to rural areas, especially Alizai village, while ensuring that action is carried out impartially and without discrimination.

The committee members reaffirmed their commitment to fully support the district administration’s efforts and thanked the deputy commissioner for addressing public concerns.

headline: Govt committed to protect minority communities’ rights: Kundi
description: Peshawar - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi on Saturday said Pakistan was a safe country for people of all faiths and reaffirmed the
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Peshawar - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi on Saturday said Pakistan was a safe country for people of all faiths and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the rights and welfare of minority communities.

Addressing a ceremony marking the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak at the Governor House, the governor extended warm greetings to the Sikh community and said minorities had played a vital role in Pakistan’s development and prosperity.

He said the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government stood shoulder to shoulder with minority communities and had continued to support them despite limited resources. He added that long-pending legislation concerning minority rights would be completed at the earliest.

The governor observed that previous provincial governments had failed to give due attention to the welfare of minorities, stressing that the present government was determined to ensure equal rights, protection and opportunities for all citizens.

Faisal Karim Kundi said lasting peace was essential for the province’s progress and prosperity, adding that the nation would always remember the sacrifices made by the martyrs of the Army Public School (APS), members of the public, police and security forces for the restoration of peace.

He said the government was committed to promoting sports and providing children with opportunities to participate in healthy activities, ensuring that they chose pens and playgrounds instead of guns. On the occasion, the governor also cut a cake to celebrate the 557th birth anniversary of Baba Guru Nanak.

Those present at the ceremony included Sardar Parwinder Singh, Sunni Sindh, Qari Roohullah Madini, Rizwanullah from the Human Rights Department and other participants. The governor was also presented with a traditional shawl.

headline: Gomal University VC calls for unity to address institutional challenges
description: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: - Gomal University Vice Chancellor (VC) Prof Dr Shakeebullah has called upon faculty members and administrative officers to set aside
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: - Gomal University Vice Chancellor (VC) Prof Dr Shakeebullah has called upon faculty members and administrative officers to set aside differences, avoid mutual blame and work collectively for the betterment of the institution and its employees.

He was addressing a reception hosted in his honour by faculty members and administrative officers at the Senate Hall of Gomal University.

The VC described the university as their alma mater and a source of pride, saying that its prevailing circumstances were concerning and required collective efforts to overcome the challenges facing the institution. He termed the placement of a vice chancellor on forced leave unfortunate and stressed that no vice chancellor wished to see the institution embroiled in problems and administrative difficulties. He said teamwork was essential for resolving institutional and employees’ issues.

Recalling his previous tenure, Prof Dr Shakeebullah said he was grateful to Allah Almighty that, through collective efforts, faculty members and officers had been granted promotions and the university had witnessed a record increase in student enrolment. He added that no employee had faced any inquiry during that period.

He said the provincial government had entrusted him with an important responsibility, which could only be fulfilled effectively through teamwork and mutual cooperation. He assured the university community that his office and doors remained open to everyone, welcoming constructive suggestions and positive thinking while making it clear that negative attitudes would not be tolerated.

Highlighting the need to strengthen the university’s financial position, he said the prevailing situation in the region demanded a positive approach and concerted efforts to secure additional resources and facilities for the institution.

headline: Sindh outlines climate investment opportunities ahead of COP31
description: KARACHI - A workshop aimed at exploring new investment opportunities to mitigate the effects of climate change and protect the environment held ahead of the
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
KARACHI - A workshop aimed at exploring new investment opportunities to mitigate the effects of climate change and protect the environment held ahead of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Sindh Environment Secretary Faisal Ahmed Uqaili, Lahore High Court Justice Jawad Hassan, Karachi Centre for Climate Change founding director Bilal Sohail, and a large number of representatives from government institutions, the investment community, environmental experts and other relevant sectors attended the workshop.

Participants held detailed discussions on various environmental initiatives, including access to clean water, restoration of agricultural land and orchards, reduction of industrial pollution and carbon emissions, promotion of electric vehicles and transparency in carbon projects.

Opening the dialogue, K4C founding director Bilal Sohail stressed the need to translate Pakistan’s climate commitments into practical projects and investment opportunities. He said effective measures in the water, energy and carbon sectors, along with private-sector participation, were essential for an industrial and coastal city like Karachi.

Lahore High Court Justice Jawad Hassan highlighted the importance of effective environmental legislation, protection of public interest and a clear regulatory framework to address climate change. He said legal certainty was essential to encourage private-sector investment, adding that laws and policies must ensure environmental protection while providing investors with clear guidance and confidence.

Speaking on the occasion, Faisal Ahmed Uqaili outlined the Sindh government’s initiatives to address climate change, protect the environment and strengthen policymaking, institutional reforms and practical interventions.

He said the provincial government had approved 13 carbon-market projects and forwarded them to the federal Ministry of Climate Change. These projects had the potential to reduce emissions equivalent to 330.13 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

The projects include wind power, emission reduction in the energy sector, production of biochar from agricultural waste, reduction of methane emissions and sustainable forestry initiatives.

He added that the Sindh government had also prepared six priority climate projects worth $62.15 million. These include biogas projects in five districts, floating agriculture in lower Sindh, reduction of carbon emissions from brick kilns and capacity-building initiatives in climate finance.

Uqaili said Sindh faced serious climate-related threats, including extreme heat, floods, water scarcity, rising sea levels and seawater intrusion into coastal areas. Addressing these challenges required joint efforts by the government, private sector and international development partners.

He said Sindh’s provincial recommendations for the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0) had been prepared, while work was also under way on a digital climate registry and dashboard to monitor carbon emissions and assess the performance of climate projects.

The secretary said the provincial government believed in guiding and supporting industrial development alongside enforcing environmental laws. In this regard, memorandums of understanding had also been signed with various educational institutions to promote research and collaboration.

Participants appreciated the Sindh government’s environmental initiatives and policies and expressed hope that the province’s experience and measures would contribute towards positive progress in addressing climate change at COP31.

The 31st Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC will be held in Antalya, Turkiye, from Nov 9 to 20, 2026. Heads of state, government representatives, experts and officials from relevant institutions from across the world are expected to attend.

Pakistan will also present its national climate priorities and position at the conference, with representation from both federal and provincial governments. Discussions will focus on addressing the impacts of climate change, environmental protection, investment in climate projects, climate adaptation and strengthening international cooperation.

PESHAWAR - Three people lost their lives and 14 others sustained serious injuries when a passenger van overturned near Rashakai Interchange on Saturday, police confirmed.

The vehicle was travelling from Taxila to Peshawar when the accident occurred. Emergency teams and ambulances from Rescue 1122 Mardan and Nowshera rushed to the scene immediately after receiving the report.

Paramedics provided initial medical aid to the injured before transferring them to nearby hospitals for further treatment.

headline: Musadik Malik calls for preventive disaster management through space technology
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musadik Malik Saturday called for shifting Pakistan’s
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musadik Malik Saturday called for shifting Pakistan’s disaster management approach from reactive response to prevention, stressing the need to harness space technology, satellite imagery, radar and hyperspectral data, artificial intelligence and advanced predictive modelling to identify risks before they turn into disasters.

Addressing the closing ceremony of the five-day UN/ Pakistan International Conference on “Leveraging Space Technology for Early Warning for All (EW4All), Climate Action and Disaster Risk Assessment,” hosted by the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO), the minister emphasized that scientific data must be translated into practical and timely interventions to prevent loss of life and property.

Drawing an analogy with cardiology, Dr. Musadik Malik said that just as early diagnosis and timely treatment could prevent a patient from requiring surgery, scientific monitoring and accurate forecasting should help prevent disasters and minimize their impact.

He highlighted Pakistan’s growing space capabilities and stressed that a warning without a specific address was effectively a warning addressed to no one. He called for moving beyond broad regional forecasts towards precise, location-specific alerts that could reach individual households and vulnerable communities.

The minister called for annual satellite-based reports on floodplains and encroachments, stronger coordination among institutions and across borders, accurate mapping of disaster-prone areas and greater engagement of young innovators through collaborative research, hackathons and innovation initiatives.

He emphasized that science must serve humanity and that rescue operations should be the last resort rather than the first response, with the protection of vulnerable people remaining the ultimate purpose of technology.

The five-day conference concluded in Islamabad, bringing together around 250 participants from across Pakistan, including representatives of federal and provincial ministries, academia and relevant national institutions, alongside delegates and representatives from 22 countries.

The broad participation reflected strong national and international engagement and a shared commitment to strengthening space-based early warning systems, climate action and disaster risk reduction.

The closing ceremony was also attended by Chairman SUPARCO and President of the Inter-Islamic Network on Space Sciences and Technology (ISNET), Muhammad Yousaf Khan; Lorant Czaran, Director, Space Applications, United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA); the Secretary, Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination; the Secretary, Rehabilitation Department, Government of Sindh; and representatives of the United Nations Platform for Space-based Information for Disaster Management and Emergency Response (UN-SPIDER), Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organization (APSCO), ISNET, Kazakhstan Gharysh Sapary and other international organizations, along with distinguished delegates and participants.

In his address, Chairman SUPARCO Muhammad Yousaf Khan emphasized that the real value of satellite technology lay in translating space-based information into timely decisions and practical action.

He highlighted three key priorities emerging from the conference: integrating information into decision-making processes, strengthening interoperable systems and data-sharing arrangements, and sustaining institutional and human resource capacities.

Addressing the ceremony, Lorant Czaran, Director, Space Applications, UNOOSA, highlighted the importance of international cooperation and the effective utilization of space-based technologies in addressing global climate and disaster-related challenges.

He acknowledged the significance of collaborative initiatives and knowledge-sharing platforms in strengthening countries’ capacities to utilize space applications for sustainable development and disaster management.

The conference featured 17 sessions, comprising two high-level plenary sessions, five panel discussions and 10 technical sessions. The technical sessions included 67 presentations delivered by national and international participants.

Furthermore, 10 keynote talks were delivered by distinguished experts, while 32 panelists contributed to discussions on critical issues concerning space technology-based climate intelligence, climate action, disaster risk reduction, the Sendai Framework, the Paris Agreement and the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) initiative.

The deliberations underscored the growing importance of satellite-based Earth observation, geospatial information and advanced space applications in strengthening multi-hazard early warning systems, assessing climate vulnerabilities, monitoring environmental changes and supporting informed decision-making.

Participants emphasized the need to translate space-based information into actionable intelligence, strengthen institutional capacities, enhance regional and international cooperation and ensure that timely warnings reached vulnerable communities.

During the closing ceremony, a comprehensive summary of the conference proceedings and key recommendations was presented, highlighting the major outcomes and areas for future collaboration.

SUPARCO also presented its Pakistan Space4Climate Initiative, reaffirming its commitment to leveraging national space capabilities and satellite-based applications to support climate monitoring, disaster risk assessment and national resilience.

The conference concluded with a renewed commitment to harnessing space technology, scientific innovation and international partnerships to strengthen climate resilience, improve disaster preparedness and advance the vision of Early Warnings for All.

headline: KP adviser urges media to verify polio reports before publication
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Area Development Secretariat Mahmood Jan Babar on Saturday urged journalists and social media users to verify information
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Area Development Secretariat Mahmood Jan Babar on Saturday urged journalists and social media users to verify information about polio from relevant health authorities before sharing it.

He warned that unsubstantiated reports could undermine vaccination campaigns and create unnecessary fear among parents.

In a video statement, he said polio was a highly sensitive public health issue directly linked to children’s health and future.

He cautioned that spreading unverified reports and rumours could weaken efforts to protect children against the crippling disease.

He observed that some social media users and journalists shared information about polio without verifying facts, stressing the need for responsible reporting, particularly on health-related matters.

Mahmood Jan said medical and scientific evidence supported the safety and effectiveness of polio vaccines.

He added that a child’s sudden illness should not be attributed to polio or a reaction to vaccine drops without proper medical investigation.

He explained that polio diagnosis involved a formal medical and laboratory examination process, while any suspected adverse reaction to vaccination also required proper assessment by qualified health professionals.

The adviser warned that misleading information could frighten parents and discourage them from allowing their children to receive polio drops.

He said cooperation among the media, health department and public was essential to protect children from the crippling disease, adding that safeguarding their health and future remained a shared responsibility.

headline: CICG releases report on China’s poverty alleviation experience
description: ISLAMABAD - The CICG Centre for Europe and Asia (China Pictorial Publications) released a report examining international perspectives on
author: INP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The CICG Centre for Europe and Asia (China Pictorial Publications) released a report examining international perspectives on China’s poverty alleviation achievements, philosophy and experience during the 2026 China-South Asia Forum on Poverty Reduction and Development Cooperation.

Qiao Zhenqi, Director of New Media Operations at the CICG Centre for Europe and Asia, formally launched the report, titled International Public Opinions on the Achievements, Philosophy, and Experience of China’s Poverty Alleviation, Gwadar Pro reported.

The report examines international perspectives on China’s poverty alleviation efforts across four dimensions: achievements, institutional governance, underlying philosophy and development experience.

Organized by CICG and Understanding China Forum (UCF), the event brought together Pakistani and Chinese officials, development experts and representatives of international organisations to discuss poverty reduction, inclusive development and opportunities for regional cooperation.

Thematic sessions explored poverty reduction practices, inclusive development, regional cooperation and emerging sources of economic growth.

The discussions highlighted the importance of effective governance, technological innovation and regional partnerships in advancing sustainable development and poverty reduction across South Asia.

headline: Solution to Balochistan’s problems not guns but education, dialogue: Bugti
description: Quetta - Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti on Saturday said that loyalty to Pakistan was unconditional, adding that some quarters were
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Quetta - Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti on Saturday said that loyalty to Pakistan was unconditional, adding that some quarters were spreading confusion and misleading narratives under the pretext of highlighting Balochistan’s case and the genuine problems faced by its people.

He said Balochistan was currently facing three major challenges: narratives justifying violence, armed terrorism and the spread of misleading information among young people through social media. He added that terrorists were destroying the province’s infrastructure and killing innocent Pakistanis.

He maintained that neither deprivation nor political differences could justify violence, stressing that the solution to Balochistan’s problems lay not in taking up arms but in education, dialogue, political engagement and democratic attitudes.

He expressed these views while addressing the convocation of the University of Management and Technology (UMT) in Lahore.

Bugti said that the people of Balochistan were equal citizens of Pakistan and that it was important to understand the province’s genuine problems, sense of deprivation and development needs. However, he added, these issues could not be used to support or justify separatist violence.

He said some quarters linked backwardness, deprivation and other challenges to armed violence to promote narratives that obscured the facts.

The Chief Minister said observers and analysts discussing the situation in Balochistan had a responsibility to speak on the basis of facts rather than attempting to make violence acceptable in any way.

He said the second major challenge facing Balochistan was armed violence, with terrorists operating in armed groups, targeting people, killing innocent citizens and destroying the province’s infrastructure.

Terrorism not only resulted in the loss of precious human lives but also hindered development, economic activities, education and efforts to secure a better future for the people of Balochistan, he added.

He said every citizen had the right to express dissent and make political demands, but imposing one’s views on others through the use of guns was unacceptable.

Highlighting the third major challenge, Bugti said young people, particularly the younger generation, were being exposed to misleading information and negative propaganda through social media. He urged the youth to evaluate every news report, claim and narrative on the basis of research and facts.

He maintained that the role of universities and educational institutions was not limited to awarding degrees but also included preparing informed, responsible citizens with critical-thinking skills who could play a positive role in society.

Appreciating the scholarships offered by UMT to students from Balochistan, Bugti said he was pleased to learn that the university had provided higher education opportunities to the province’s youth.

He described the Punjab government’s annual allocation of Rs1 billion for promoting education in Balochistan as a valuable example of inter-provincial cooperation and national solidarity.

Such initiatives not only provided opportunities for students from Balochistan to pursue higher education but also strengthened trust and mutual relations among the provinces, he added.

He said the Balochistan government was striving to provide scholarships covering 80 per cent of educational expenses to more than 80 per cent of its students, ensuring that a lack of financial resources did not prevent talented young people from pursuing higher education.

“Our efforts are aimed at providing quality education, modern skills and equal development opportunities to the youth of Balochistan,” he said, adding that investing in young people’s education was an investment in the bright future of Balochistan and Pakistan.

The Chief Minister said the youth of Balochistan were talented and could play an effective role in national development if provided with appropriate opportunities, guidance and educational facilities.

He said education was the most effective means of steering young people away from extremism, violence and misleading ideologies and towards knowledge, awareness and constructive activities.

He stressed the need to show the younger generation a path of hope, hard work and progress instead of allowing them to fall prey to despair and negative propaganda.

Congratulating the graduating students, their parents and teachers, Bugti said graduation was not the end of a journey but the beginning of a new and important phase of practical life.

He said the graduates were entering a new world where continuous hard work, honesty and consistency were essential for success. He urged them to improve their skills, set ambitious goals and use their education and abilities to serve the country and the nation.

Bugti thanked the university administration, faculty members and management for inviting him to the convocation, saying it was an honour for him to attend the event.

headline: Citizens demand action to remove encroachments from graveyard land
description: Mardan - Citizens have expressed concern over the lack of effective action against alleged encroachments and illegal occupations of graveyard land in
author: Riaz Khan
article_text:
Mardan - Citizens have expressed concern over the lack of effective action against alleged encroachments and illegal occupations of graveyard land in various parts of Mardan city and its surrounding areas.

Residents have urged the district administration, the municipal corporation and other relevant authorities to launch an immediate and indiscriminate operation to remove encroachments and illegal occupations from graveyard land. According to local residents, even graveyards have not been spared by the “land mafia”, with reports of illegal occupations and encroachments emerging from several locations. Graveyards are sacred places where people lay their loved ones to rest. The occupation of burial land and the blocking of access routes not only cause distress to the public but could also lead to a shortage of burial space for future generations.

Citizens have pointed out that while the administration occasionally conducts anti-encroachment drives in various parts of the city, a dedicated campaign is urgently needed to protect graveyard land. They have suggested conducting a comprehensive survey of all graveyards in the city and its suburbs, determining their original boundaries, verifying them against official government records and removing all illegal occupations.

Members of the public have urged the Commissioner of Mardan Division, the Deputy Commissioner, Assistant Commissioners and TMA officials to investigate alleged encroachments on graveyard land, initiate legal action against those responsible and introduce permanent measures to protect these burial grounds. Citizens have also questioned when a formal operation against encroachments in Mardan’s graveyards will finally begin. They have demanded that, instead of ignoring the issue, the authorities take immediate and practical steps to uphold the sanctity of graveyards and protect public land.

headline: Samar Bilour condemns attack on Mansehra AC, mourns Rashakai accident victims
description: Peshawar - Advisor to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations, Samar Haroon Bilour, has expressed serious concern
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Advisor to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations, Samar Haroon Bilour, has expressed serious concern over the firing incident targeting Assistant Commissioner Mansehra Adil Waseem in Panakot, Tehsil Pabbi, Nowshera.

In a statement, she expressed regret over the injuries sustained by Assistant Commissioner Adil Waseem and prayed for his speedy and complete recovery. She directed the relevant authorities to ensure the provision of the best possible medical facilities to the injured officer and called for a transparent and impartial investigation into the incident. She further stressed that those involved in the attack must be arrested without delay and brought to justice.

She said ensuring the safety and security of public officials and citizens was a fundamental responsibility of the relevant authorities. Effective measures were essential to maintain law and order and protect the lives and property of the public. She also appreciated the timely response and provision of medical assistance by Rescue 1122 Nowshera.

Meanwhile, Samar Bilour expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic road accident near Rashakai Interchange in Mardan, which claimed three lives and left 14 others injured.

She extended her heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and expressed solidarity with them in their hour of grief. She prayed that Allah Almighty grant eternal peace to the departed souls and give patience and strength to their families. She also prayed for the speedy and complete recovery of the injured and stressed that they should be provided with the best possible medical treatment.

Expressing concern over the increasing number of road accidents, she said preventing such incidents was a collective responsibility. She emphasised the importance of thoroughly inspecting vehicles before every journey, particularly their tyres, brakes and other essential mechanical and safety components.

She further observed that negligence and carelessness could lead to the tragic loss of precious human lives.

She stressed that effectively regulating the traffic system, ensuring vehicle fitness, maintaining safety standards and enforcing traffic laws were shared responsibilities of all relevant authorities.

She called for effective monitoring and concrete measures to prevent road accidents and safeguard human lives.

She said ensuring the safety and security of public officials and citizens was a fundamental responsibility of the relevant authorities. Effective measures were essential to maintain law and order and protect the lives and property of the public. She also appreciated the timely response and provision of medical assistance by Rescue 1122 Nowshera.
Meanwhile, Samar Bilour expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic road accident near Rashakai Interchange in Mardan, which claimed three lives and left 14 others injured.

She extended her heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and expressed solidarity with them in their hour of grief. She prayed that Allah Almighty grant eternal peace to the departed souls and give patience and strength to their families. She also prayed for the speedy and complete recovery of the injured and stressed that they should be provided with the best possible medical treatment.

Expressing concern over the increasing number of road accidents, she said preventing such incidents was a collective responsibility. She emphasised the importance of thoroughly inspecting vehicles before every journey, particularly their tyres, brakes and other essential mechanical and safety components.
She further observed that negligence and carelessness could lead to the tragic loss of precious human lives.

She stressed that effectively regulating the traffic system, ensuring vehicle fitness, maintaining safety standards and enforcing traffic laws were shared responsibilities of all relevant authorities.
She called for effective monitoring and concrete measures to prevent road accidents and safeguard human lives.

headline: ANF arrests 10 drug suppliers, over 33kg of drugs seized
description: Rawalpindi - Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) has arrested 10 drug suppliers and recovered 33.8 kilograms of drugs during seven operations conducted in
author: APP
article_text:
Rawalpindi - Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) has arrested 10 drug suppliers and recovered 33.8 kilograms of drugs during seven operations conducted in different cities across the country.

According to ANF spokesperson, during an international drug interdiction operation, 2kg of hashish were recovered from the luggage of a passenger travelling to Dubai on a work visa at Bacha Khan International Airport. The passenger was arrested.

In inter-provincial operations, 12kg of ice were seized from two suppliers travelling on a passenger bus near Sher Shah Toll Plaza in Multan. In another operation near Karnal Sher Khan Interchange in Swabi, 10.8kg of opium was recovered from a vehicle, leading to the arrest of two individuals.

During domestic operations, 6kg of hashish concealed inside a motorcycle was recovered near the GT Road Bridge in Peshawar, and the accused was arrested. In another operation near Sector D-17/2 Markaz, Islamabad, 2.4kg of hashish was seized from two suspects.

Similarly, 260 grams of hashish were recovered from two motorcyclists on GT Road in Jhelum, while 400 grams of a prohibited substance concealed inside a juicer machine in a parcel were seized at a private courier office in Sector I-9, Islamabad.

Cases have been registered against the arrested individuals under the Control of Narcotic Substances Act (CNSA), 1997.

headline: RPO, CPO pin rank badges on 41 promoted inspectors in Rawalpindi
description: Rawalpindi - Regional Police Officer (RPO) Babar Sarfraz Alpa and City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera pinned rank badges on newly
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Rawalpindi - Regional Police Officer (RPO) Babar Sarfraz Alpa and City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera pinned rank badges on newly promoted inspectors at a ceremony held in Rawalpindi on Saturday.

A total of 41 sub-inspectors across the Rawalpindi region were recently elevated to the rank of Inspector in accordance with directives issued by the Inspector General of Police (IGP) Punjab. Speaking on the occasion, RPO Babar Sarfraz Alpa congratulated the officers, stating that departmental promotion serves as official recognition of hard work, dedication, and professional service. He emphasized that promotion brings added responsibility, urging officers to discharge their duties with heightened devotion and integrity.

“Promoted officers must treat the protection of citizens’ lives and property, alongside crime prevention, as their primary duty,” RPO Alpa said, directing them to utilize all available capabilities to ensure the rule of law and the timely provision of justice to the public. He also stressed the importance of polite behavior, courtesy, and a spirit of public service when interacting with citizens.

CPO Sukhera noted that achieving the rank of inspector represents a major career milestone. He encouraged the officers to fulfill their new assignments with diligence, professional competence, and dedication, adding that regular promotions boost morale and enhance the overall operational efficiency of the police department. The officers promoted to the rank of inspector include Waheed Imtiaz, Amjad Ali, Naseer Ahmed, Muhammad Safeer, Nadeem Akhtar, Wajid Muneer, Muhammad Noman, Muhammad Irfan, Mohsin Mehmood Qureshi, Jaan Muhammad, Muhammad Aslam, Farooq Akhtar, Bilal Amjad, Muhammad Javed Jamal, Jamal Nawaz, Muhammad Ali, Arslan Ahsan, Syed Zaka-ul-Hassan, Muhammad Waleed Iftikhar, Ali Abbas, Shafique Ahmed Malik, Raja Yousaf Mehmood, Nabeel, Faisal Amin, Muhammad Sajid, Maqbool Hussain, Muhammad Shafique, Mehboob Hussain, Aurangzeb, Irfan Mansab, Shamsheer Ahmed, Hajra Awan, Syeda Shabana Batool, Wajid Khan, Muhammad Adeel, Mukhtar Ahmed, Hassan Raza, Safdar Hussain, and Muneer Ahmed.

headline: The Millennium Education hosts MQCAP 2026
description: ISLAMABAD - The Millennium Education Group successfully hosted its annual flagship Millennium Qualification, Curriculum & Assessment Programme
author: PR
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Millennium Education Group successfully hosted its annual flagship Millennium Qualification, Curriculum & Assessment Programme MQCAP 2026, under the theme “ELEVATE – Leadership for Impact,” at Future World School, DHA Phase 5, Islamabad, bringing together 170 academic leaders from across Pakistan to advance educational excellence, innovation and school leadership.

The distinguished gathering included Principals, School Heads and Academic Coordinators from The Millennium Education Group nationwide network for a dynamic day of professional learning, strategic dialogue and collaborative engagement aimed at strengthening educational leadership and improving teaching and learning outcomes.

Organised by the Millennium Institute of Professional Development MIPD, a department of The Millennium Education Group, MQCAP serves as a strategic platform for advancing academic excellence, curriculum innovation, assessment practices, educational technology and institutional capacity building.

The initiative reflects the visionary leadership of Dr. Faisal Mushtaq, Chairman & CEO of The Millennium Education Group, whose unwavering commitment to educational excellence, innovation and future-ready learning continues to shape the organisation’s progressive educational philosophy.

His vision emphasises empowering academic leaders, strengthening professional accountability and fostering a culture of continuous institutional improvement.

Organised under the academic direction of Ms Amna Salik, MQCAP 2026 provided an enriching platform for academic leaders to exchange perspectives, explore emerging educational practices and translate institutional vision into meaningful classroom and school-wide impact.

Strengthening Academic Leadership and Educational Quality

A central focus of MQCAP 2026 was strengthening academic leadership through effective curriculum planning, learner-centred pedagogy, differentiated instruction and measurable learning outcomes. Participants explored strategies for enhancing instructional effectiveness, promoting professional collaboration and ensuring consistent academic standards across TME institutions nationwide.

Advancing Assessment and Evidence-Informed Improvement

The programme highlighted the importance of diagnostic, formative and summative assessments, academic quality assurance, constructive feedback and data-driven decision-making. Discussions emphasised using assessment not merely to measure student achievement but as a powerful tool for identifying learning gaps, improving instructional practices and supporting individual learner needs. Recognising the transformative role of technology, MQCAP 2026 explored educational technologies, digital learning platforms, Google for Education tools and innovative technology-integration models.

The sessions reinforced the importance of aligning digital transformation with meaningful pedagogical objectives to enhance student engagement, creativity, collaboration and inclusive learning experiences.

Professional development remained a cornerstone of MQCAP 2026, with discussions focusing on internationally recognised professional qualifications, mentoring, reflective teaching practices and collaborative learning communities. Participants examined how sustained investment in teacher development and leadership competencies contributes to stronger educational institutions and improved student outcomes.

Reflecting the theme “ELEVATE – Leadership for Impact,” the programme encouraged participating academic leaders to move beyond professional learning towards purposeful action. headline: District admin warns against fake reporting on anti-dengue actions amidst low number of patients
description: Rawalpindi - Punjab government has reiterated a zero-tolerance policy against negligence, absenteeism, and fake reporting in the ongoing
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Rawalpindi - Punjab government has reiterated a zero-tolerance policy against negligence, absenteeism, and fake reporting in the ongoing anti-dengue drive, directing immediate disciplinary action against delinquent officials.

The warning was issued by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Social Services) Fazail Mudassar while presiding over a meeting of the District Emergency and Response Committee (DERC) for dengue prevention at the deputy commissioner’s office in Rawalpindi. The district health officer (DHO) alongside senior officials from front-line departments attended the meeting.

The committee reviewed the overall performance of the anti-dengue campaign, current patient statistics, indoor and outdoor surveillance, larva identification, hotspot management, and field team operations.

During the briefing, officials revealed that Rawalpindi recorded 83 confirmed dengue cases up to October 30, 2026, marking a drastic reduction compared to the 1,586 cases reported during the corresponding period last year.

To achieve this drop, health and municipal teams conducted indoor and outdoor surveillance across approximately 5.875 million households and over 2 million commercial and public sites this year, detecting and eliminating dengue larvae at more than 241,000 locations.

Addressing the session, ADC Mudassar noted that while the dengue situation remains under control this season, the final 20 days of the campaign are critical. He urged all administrative bodies to intensify field activities without dropping their guard.

“Absenteeism of field staff, reporting of fake activities, and poor performance will not be tolerated under any circumstances,” Mudassar stated, instructing department heads to identify negligent personnel immediately for administrative proceedings.

He ordered strict monitoring of high-risk hotspots, rapid response upon larvae detection, and mandatory geo-tagging for all field operations. He further directed officials to clear all pending Dengue Vector Response (DVR) reports without delay.

Closing the meeting, the ADC called for sustained, coordinated actions across departments to pool available resources and prevent any late-season spike in vector-borne infections.

headline: 447,614 children to be vaccinated in capital
description: ISLAMABAD - The Sub-National Immunization Days (SNID) polio campaign was inaugurated on Saturday at Golra Station, with health teams set to administer polio
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Sub-National Immunization Days (SNID) polio campaign was inaugurated on Saturday at Golra Station, with health teams set to administer polio drops to 447,614 children across Islamabad.

District Health Officer Islamabad Dr Syeda Rashida Batool accompanied the Deputy Commissioner Islamabad at the inauguration ceremony. The campaign aims to protect children under five years of age against poliovirus through door-to-door vaccination and ensure that no child is missed.

Parents have been urged to cooperate with vaccination teams and ensure that every child under five receives polio drops during the campaign to help protect them against the crippling disease.

headline: MIH holds breast cancer awareness session
description: ISLAMABAD - Maroof International Hospital (MIH), in collaboration with the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA), has organized a health awareness session for the
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Maroof International Hospital (MIH), in collaboration with the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA), has organized a health awareness session for the aviation community, highlighting the importance of early breast cancer detection and mental well-being.

The session was attended by personnel from the CAA, Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), Airports Security Force (ASF), Customs and various airlines.

Consultant Breast Cancer Surgeon Dr Saira Mahmood and Consultant Psychologist and Psychotherapist Dr Nargis Nawaz addressed participants, highlighting the importance of timely screening, early detection and appropriate medical consultation.

The speakers also discussed mental health challenges, the need to recognize early warning signs and the importance of breaking the stigma associated with psychological well-being.

Participants were encouraged to promote health awareness among their families and colleagues and adopt preventive healthcare practices.

The initiative aimed to encourage a culture of care in workplaces by placing equal emphasis on physical health and mental well-being.

headline: 4 held for posing as army ‘Majors’ to con ride-hailing drivers
description: ISLAMABAD - A ride is booked on the InDrive app, with the drop-off point near a military hospital, GHQ or an army base. Minutes later, the
author: Haris Shirazi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - A ride is booked on the InDrive app, with the drop-off point near a military hospital, GHQ or an army base. Minutes later, the driver’s phone rings. The caller introduces himself as an army officer, said Major Syed Iftikhar, and says a family member needs urgent medical treatment.

That, according to the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), was how a gang cheated ride-hailing and delivery drivers in Islamabad. Four suspects have been arrested, and an Islamabad court has given investigators two days’ physical remand.

The FIR names the suspects as Muhammad Mohsin, Muhammad Bilal and Muhammad Aslam, all residents of Tehsil Sillanwali in Sargodha district, and Syed Zahid Abbass. It was registered on Oct 29 at the NCCIA’s Cyber Crime Reporting Centre (CCRC) in Islamabad on the complaint of Muhammad Iftikhar.

According to the FIR, the accused used fake SIM cards and WhatsApp accounts, each under a different dummy name, and sent drivers fake army service cards to establish their credentials. Drivers were asked to send money through branchless banking accounts for hospital bills or other emergencies, with a promise of reimbursement and extra payment at the drop-off point. Once the money was transferred, the accused cancelled the ride or order and became unreachable.

Investigators traced two of the SIM numbers to a Wateen Telecom internet connection registered in the name of Muhammad Aslam. The NCCIA says both numbers were found logged in on the accused’s phones, and that the money was traced to four mobile banking accounts.

Officials privy to the investigation told The Nation that the case surfaced when a victim reported the fraud to the NCCIA, which then worked on the complaint, traced the locations of the suspects and arrested them. They said the scale of the fraud became clear during interrogation. The suspects had been running the scam since 2022, the amounts involved are far larger than initially believed, and the proceeds were invested in a house, four shops, a few plots and four cars, including an MG and a Honda City. The officials said the maximum punishment in case of conviction is seven years.

The accused were produced before Senior Civil Judge/ Judicial Magistrate (Sec-30, West) Malak Aman, who granted two days’ physical remand to Investigating Officer Babar Ali. They are to be produced again on Sunday. The case is registered under the cyber crime law and the Pakistan Penal Code’s provisions on cheating, impersonation and common intention, and the FIR says the role of others, if any, will be determined during the investigation.

headline: Amir Muqam congratulates Gilgit-Baltistan people on 79th Independence Day
description: Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and SAFRON Engineer Amir Muqam has congratulated the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on their 79th
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and SAFRON Engineer Amir Muqam has congratulated the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on their 79th Independence Day, being observed on November 1.

In his special message, the minister said the people of Gilgit-Baltistan had the unique distinction of celebrating independence twice a year, on August 14 and November 1, with the latter marking the region’s liberation and accession to Pakistan.

He paid tribute to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan for their struggle and sacrifices and expressed solidarity with the people of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir and Palestine.

Muqam said the people of Kashmir had been struggling for their right to self-determination for the past eight decades. He also appreciated the role of the Pakistan Armed Forces in protecting the country's borders and sovereignty, saying they had foiled attempts to destabilise Pakistan and effectively responded to acts of aggression.

Highlighting the strategic importance of Gilgit-Baltistan in the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), the minister said the federal government attached great importance to the region's development.

He said the government, in collaboration with the Gilgit-Baltistan administration, would continue development initiatives, particularly focusing on youth empowerment and the promotion of tourism.

Muqam observed that Gilgit-Baltistan had immense tourism potential and its development would remain a priority for the federal government.

He also highlighted development projects undertaken by the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) during its previous tenures and reaffirmed the government's commitment to the region's progress and prosperity.

The minister called for collective efforts to ensure the sustainable development of Gilgit-Baltistan and Pakistan.

headline: Pakistan urges Afghan Taliban to act against militant groups
description: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoIB), in a statement issued on Saturday, criticised a recent social media post by the Afghan Taliban
author: NNI
article_text:
Pakistan has said that the Afghan Taliban must take decisive action against militant groups operating from Afghan soil, describing their continued presence as the main obstacle to improved bilateral relations.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MoIB), in a statement issued on Saturday, criticised a recent social media post by the Afghan Taliban spokesperson, saying it reflected Kabul's misguided approach and failure to address the root causes of deteriorating relations between the two countries.

The ministry said the Taliban leadership continued to blame Islamabad's policies while ignoring the persistent threat of terrorism emanating from Afghan territory.

Reiterating Pakistan's position, the ministry said terrorism was a red line and the security of its citizens was non-negotiable. It added that Pakistan would not tolerate cross-border terrorist sanctuaries or allow its citizens to remain targets of militant groups operating from Afghanistan.

The statement said Pakistan reserved the right to take all necessary measures to eliminate threats to its national security under international law, regardless of their origin.

It stressed that the responsibility for addressing these security threats rested with the Afghan Taliban regime, adding that Pakistan's resolve to protect its people should not be mistaken for weakness.

The ministry identified the Taliban government's continued failure to act against militant factions as the principal obstacle to normalising relations between the two neighbouring countries.

It further said that shifting blame, making assurances and questioning Pakistan's policies would neither resolve the crisis nor absolve Kabul of its responsibilities.

The statement warned that Pakistan's security would not be held hostage to what it described as Kabul's inaction, evasions or misplaced priorities.

headline: Asifa Bhutto Zardari felicitates Gilgit-Baltistan people on Independence Day
description: First Lady Asifa Bhutto Zardari has extended her warm greetings to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan, particularly its youth, girls and women, on the occasion of
author: NNI
article_text:
First Lady Asifa Bhutto Zardari has extended her warm greetings to the people of Gilgit-Baltistan, particularly its youth, girls and women, on the occasion of the region's 79th Independence Day.

In her message on Sunday, she paid tribute to those who liberated the region from Dogra rule, acknowledging their courage and sacrifices in shaping its future alongside Pakistan.

She said the legacy of their struggle must be honoured by ensuring access to education, meaningful employment opportunities and greater participation of women in decision-making.

Referring to the contributions of Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto and the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), she said their efforts reflected a commitment to ensuring dignity, representation and self-governance for the people of Gilgit-Baltistan.

The first lady particularly emphasised the importance of empowering girls and women, saying every girl deserved the opportunity and support to pursue her ambitions, whether in education, science, healthcare, entrepreneurship, sports or public service.

She called for practical measures, including quality schools, trained teachers, scholarships, safe transport, digital access and improved healthcare facilities, particularly in remote mountainous communities.

Asifa also stressed the need to improve maternal healthcare, nutrition and women's wellbeing, saying these should remain central to the region's development.

Highlighting the potential of Gilgit-Baltistan's youth, she said they could contribute significantly to tourism, technology, agriculture, sports and entrepreneurship if provided with appropriate skills, reliable internet connectivity and access to finance and markets.

She also called for greater recognition and economic opportunities for women engaged in handicrafts, small businesses and agriculture.

The first lady emphasised that young people and women should be included in efforts to protect the region's mountains, glaciers, rivers and cultural heritage, saying their participation was essential for building safer communities and preserving the environment.

She concluded by expressing hope for a prosperous Gilgit-Baltistan where girls could grow with confidence, women could live with dignity and young people could look forward to a brighter future.

headline: Lahore tops global pollution rankings with AQI of 448
description: Lahore has become the world's most polluted city, with its overall Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching a hazardous level of 448 amid severe smog, according to
author: NNI
article_text:
Lahore has become the world's most polluted city, with its overall Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching a hazardous level of 448 amid severe smog, according to Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) sources on Sunday.

Air quality data showed alarming pollution levels across several localities, with Iqbal Town recording the highest AQI of 617.

Paragon City recorded an AQI of 513, followed by Model Town at 453, Chaman Park at 430, Barki Road at 427 and DHA Phase 5 at 324.

Health and environmental experts have advised residents to take precautionary measures, including wearing face masks when going outdoors and avoiding unnecessary travel, particularly during early morning and late evening hours.

Citizens have also been urged to limit outdoor activities and avoid prolonged exposure to polluted air.

Experts warned that severe smog could cause eye irritation, nasal and throat discomfort, breathing difficulties and serious respiratory illnesses.

Children, elderly people and individuals with existing respiratory conditions have been advised to take extra precautions.

In view of the worsening air quality, authorities have urged residents to remain indoors unless necessary and follow official safety guidelines.

headline: Tourist influx boosts local economy in Swat's scenic valleys
description: Thousands of tourists are flocking to Swat's scenic destinations, including Kalam, Mahudhand Lake, Malam Jabba and neighbouring valleys, boosting local
author: NNI
article_text:
Thousands of tourists are flocking to Swat's scenic destinations, including Kalam, Mahudhand Lake, Malam Jabba and neighbouring valleys, boosting local businesses and creating employment opportunities as winter tourism gains momentum.

The growing influx of visitors has increased demand for hotels, guesthouses, restaurants, transport services, horse rides and photography, providing a welcome boost to the livelihoods of local communities.

Tourists are particularly attracted to the natural beauty of Kalam, Bahrain, Madyan, Osho Valley, Jazz Banda and Mahudhand Lake, where mist-covered mountains, pine forests, waterfalls and crystal-clear waters offer opportunities for sightseeing and adventure.

Local horse riders and photographers are among those benefiting from the increased tourist activity. Horseback rides along mountain trails towards Mahudhand Lake have become a popular attraction, while local photographers are earning through visitors seeking memorable pictures against the scenic mountain landscape.

The growing use of social media has also helped promote Swat's tourism potential, as visitors share photographs and videos of the region on Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, attracting more tourists.

Hotels and guesthouses in Kalam and Malam Jabba are also experiencing strong demand, with several accommodation facilities operating at or near full capacity during peak weekends.

Improved road connectivity, particularly following the opening of the Swat Motorway, has made the region more accessible to tourists travelling from major cities, including Peshawar and Islamabad.

Besides sightseeing, visitors can enjoy skiing at Malam Jabba, paragliding in Kalam, boating at Mahudhand Lake, hiking, rafting and other adventure activities.

Meanwhile, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Tourism and Culture Authority is pursuing several initiatives to promote sustainable tourism, improve accommodation facilities and develop relatively unexplored destinations.

Officials said camping pods had been established at Bamborat Kalash Valley in Chitral, Shaheed Sir in Allai, Battagram, Mahban and Malka in Buner to provide affordable accommodation.

Around 10 additional tourist sites have also been identified for camping pod facilities, including Jarogo Waterfall, Solatar and Kalam in Swat, Lashkargaz and Broghal in Chitral, Kumrat in Upper Dir, Alpuri in Shangla, Samana Top in Hangu, and Larum Top and Bin Shahi in Lower Dir.

The plans also include establishing three new ski resorts in Kaghan, Chitral and Swat to attract international tourists and adventure sports enthusiasts.

Four new hill stations are also proposed, including two in Kaghan and one each in Chitral and Abbottabad, to reduce pressure on established tourist destinations.

Other initiatives under consideration include tulip cultivation in Naran and Kaghan to create additional income opportunities for local growers, as well as the proposed Battakundi-Lalazar chairlift project.

Officials believe these initiatives could help transform tourism from a seasonal activity into a sustainable, year-round economic sector, creating more employment and business opportunities for communities across the province.

headline: Police arrest 631 professional beggars during October
description: LAHORE - Lahore Police on Saturday intensified their anti-begging campaign, arresting 631 professional beggars during October and registering cases against
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Lahore Police on Saturday intensified their anti-begging campaign, arresting 631 professional beggars during October and registering cases against them. According to police sources, Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Lahore Bilal Siddique Kamyana has directed strict enforcement of the Anti-Beggary Act across all divisions of the city to curb organized begging networks and exploitation of motorists at traffic signals. During the ongoing campaign, a total of 2,297 professional beggars, including 2,252 men and 45 women, have been arrested across Lahore so far this year. The CCPO has also directed divisional police officers and traffic police officials to maintain close surveillance of major roads and traffic signals to prevent professional beggars, swindlers and fraudsters from operating. He emphasised the need for effective enforcement measures to dismantle organized begging networks and ensure compliance with the law.

headline: TEPA seeks Rs.590m for AI-based traffic signals
description: LAHORE - The Traffic Engineering and Planning Agency (TEPA) on Saturday sought more than Rs590 million for the installation of modern artificial intelligence
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The Traffic Engineering and Planning Agency (TEPA) on Saturday sought more than Rs590 million for the installation of modern artificial intelligence (AI)-based traffic signals across the provincial capital to improve traffic flow and reduce congestion. According to official sources, TEPA has submitted a formal summary to the Punjab Housing Department for the release of funds to install automated traffic signals equipped with vehicle video detection technology. The initiative has moved forward following the successful completion of an initial pilot project, under which modern pelican traffic signals have already been activated at Adda Plot and Jati Umra Chowk. Under the proposed project, major intersections across Lahore will gradually be integrated into the advanced traffic management system to replace conventional traffic control mechanisms. The AI-based system will use cameras installed at intersections to monitor vehicle movement and assess traffic pressure in real time. Signal timings will then be adjusted automatically according to traffic volume and flow. The system will allow longer signal durations on roads experiencing heavier traffic, helping improve vehicle movement and reduce unnecessary delays at busy intersections. According to sources, TEPA was preparing to introduce technology-based traffic management solutions to address growing traffic congestion and improve the overall efficiency of the city’s road network.
