headline: JI to hold public rallies in five cities ahead of long march
description: LAHORE - Liaquat Baloch, deputy chief of Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan, has warned that the party will launch a long march from Multan to Islamabad if the
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Liaquat Baloch, deputy chief of Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan, has warned that the party will launch a long march from Multan to Islamabad if the government fails to provide relief to the public on the petroleum levy. He said final negotiations between the government and Jamaat-e-Islami on the petroleum levy would be held next week, urging the government to provide relief to the people. Baloch warned that failure to reach an agreement would lead to a long march towards Islamabad. He said public rallies would be held in Quetta, Mirpurkhas, Bahawalpur, Mansehra and Sargodha ahead of the long march to mobilise public support. He added that committees had been formed to oversee arrangements for the planned march.

headline: President Zardari, PM Shehbaz felicitate Gilgit-Baltistan on 79th Independence Day
description: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have congratulated the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on the region’s 79th Independence Day,
author: Web Desk
article_text:
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have congratulated the people of Gilgit-Baltistan on the region’s 79th Independence Day, paying tribute to those who fought against Dogra rule and secured its freedom.

In separate messages issued on Sunday, both leaders recalled the historic events of November 1, 1947, when the people of Gilgit-Baltistan ended Dogra rule, declared independence and subsequently wrote to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, seeking the region’s accession to Pakistan.

President Zardari acknowledged the contributions of Gilgit-Baltistan’s people to Pakistan’s defence and development, recognising their sacrifices and role in the country’s history.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also paid tribute to the determination, courage and sacrifices of the region’s leaders and people during the struggle for freedom.

He reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to extending full support to the Gilgit-Baltistan government in addressing economic difficulties and introducing institutional and administrative reforms.

Both leaders highlighted the historical significance of the day and reiterated their appreciation for the people who played a role in securing the region’s freedom.

headline: LGH suspends four officials over negligence
description: LAHORE - The Lahore General Hospital (LGH) administration has taken strict action against negligence, lack of interest and dereliction of duty in official
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The Lahore General Hospital (LGH) administration has taken strict action against negligence, lack of interest and dereliction of duty in official matters, suspending four officials with immediate effect and issuing a show-cause notice to the sanitary inspector. According to an LGH spokesperson on Saturday, written explanations have also been sought from three other employees over their performance and conduct. Meanwhile, AMS (Emergency) Dr Sinaan Mustafa has been replaced, while Dr Ambreen Muqaddas has been directed to assume charge as AMS Emergency (Evening). MS LGH Prof Dr Faryad Hussain has issued a formal notification in this regard. Prof Dr Faryad Hussain directed all administrative doctors to strengthen monitoring of hospital affairs to ensure uninterrupted provision of medical facilities to patients. He made it clear that negligence and carelessness in the performance of official duties would not be tolerated under any circumstances and that discipline would be maintained at all costs. The MS further directed administrative focal person doctors of all departments to ensure that sanitary staff reporting for duty wear the prescribed uniform, warning that those arriving without uniform would be marked absent. He also instructed the concerned doctors to strictly monitor cleanliness arrangements and staff attendance to ensure a clean and healthy environment for patients, reiterating that there would be no compromise on cleanliness and security.

headline: NCCIA launches awareness drive against online fraud, cyber harassment
description: LAHORE - The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) Lahore Zone on Saturday decided to expand its cybercrime awareness campaign to educational
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) Lahore Zone on Saturday decided to expand its cybercrime awareness campaign to educational institutions, social organisations and households to protect citizens, students and children from online crimes. On the directions of Additional Director Lahore Zone Atif Ameer, special awareness sessions were organised at Alkhidmat Foundation Pakistan and the University of Engineering and Technology (UET) where students and participants were briefed on online fraud, cyber harassment and ways to ensure digital safety. During the sessions, NCCIA deputy directors Waqas Saeed and Mudassar Shah highlighted various aspects of cybersecurity, online financial fraud, digital harassment, unsafe use of social media and other cybercrimes. They also explained practical measures to identify potential online threats and prevent digital fraud. At the Alkhidmat Foundation’s central office, participants included Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Khubaib Bilal, Group Chief Financial Officer Atiq Rashid and Shoaib Hashmi. In his presentation, Deputy Director Waqas Saeed highlighted fraudulent websites, suspicious links, phishing, online financial scams, cyber harassment and the illegal use of personal and institutional information. Participants were advised to use strong passwords, enable multi-factor authentication and secure their social media accounts. They were also briefed on avoiding financial fraud through fake calls and messages. At UET, the NCCIA officers briefed students on online gambling, financial fraud, phishing, misuse of digital identities and cyberbullying. They said illegal activities carried out through the internet and social media were also covered under the country’s laws and could lead to legal action against those involved. The students were also guided on immediate safety measures in case of cyberattacks or hacked accounts, including changing passwords, disconnecting affected devices from networks, preserving digital evidence and filing complaints with the relevant authorities. The speakers urged victims of online fraud and harassment to report such incidents promptly instead of remaining silent. Additional Director Atif Ameer said the awareness campaign would be extended to schools, colleges and other educational institutions, while efforts would also be made to educate children and parents about cybercrime prevention at their homes. He said public awareness and cooperation were essential for preventing cybercrimes, adding that the NCCIA would continue such activities to promote digital safety among citizens. At the conclusion of the Alkhidmat session,the foundation presented a shield to Deputy Director Waqas Saeed, while Group Chief Financial Officer Atiq Rashid thanked the NCCIA officers for their participation.

headline: 96 underground water tanks being built in 51 cities under Punjab Development Programme
description: LAHORE - Punjab Local Government Minister Zeshan Rafiq on Saturday reviewed progress on the Punjab Development Programme (PDP) and directed officials to ensure
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Punjab Local Government Minister Zeshan Rafiq on Saturday reviewed progress on the Punjab Development Programme (PDP) and directed officials to ensure completion of development targets before the next monsoon season. He was given a briefing at the Programme Management Unit (PMU), Garden Town, in the presence of Secretary Local Government Zaid Bin Maqsood, Project Director Shahid Zaman Lak, Municipal Officers Infrastructure (MOIs) and Assistant Project Directors. The minister said construction of disposal stations was underway following the completion of water tanks and drains under the programme. He said 96 underground water tanks being constructed under the “Maryam Nawaz’s Sohna Punjab” programme would provide storage capacity for 23 million gallons of rainwater in 51 cities. He added that 115 drains, stretching over 61 kilometers were also being constructed under the PDP, while work on 40 disposal stations had started in different cities. The minister directed officials to expedite land acquisition for the remaining disposal stations and make every possible effort to achieve the targets before the next monsoon season. He also directed the Municipal Officers Infrastructure to ensure timely completion of development schemes in their respective cities.

headline: PIA resumes direct flights between Islamabad and Beijing
description: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has restarted its direct flight service between Pakistan and China, with the first flight operating on October 30,
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has restarted its direct flight service between Pakistan and China, with the first flight operating on October 30, restoring air connectivity between Islamabad and Beijing.

The resumption is expected to strengthen aviation links between the two countries and reflects the national carrier’s efforts to restore and maintain regular services in the Chinese market.

Under the revised schedule, PIA will operate one weekly flight between Islamabad and Beijing every Friday, offering passengers a direct travel option between the two capitals. The airline also plans to provide competitive fares while maintaining reliable and consistent services.

As part of efforts to expand its reach across China, PIA has also strengthened cooperation with three major Chinese airlines: Air China, Shenzhen Airlines and Hainan Airlines.

The partnership with Air China will allow passengers travelling through Beijing to access onward connections to several domestic destinations across China, using the capital as a major transit hub.

headline: PM Shehbaz welcomes Pakistan’s election as G-24 chairman, calls it diplomatic milestone
description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has described Pakistan’s election as chairman of the Intergovernmental Group of Twenty-Four (G-24) as a significant
author: APP
article_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has described Pakistan’s election as chairman of the Intergovernmental Group of Twenty-Four (G-24) as a significant diplomatic achievement, saying it would strengthen the country’s role in international economic affairs.

According to a spokesperson, the prime minister expressed satisfaction over the development and praised Finance Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb and his team for their hard work, diplomatic efforts and professional expertise.

Shehbaz commended the finance minister and his team for their active engagement during the annual meetings of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), saying their efforts had helped Pakistan secure an important position in shaping economic policies for developing countries.

He said the G-24 chairmanship would give Pakistan a stronger platform to push for reforms in the international financial system, promote fairer financial support to address climate change and encourage sustainable development opportunities for emerging economies.

The prime minister added that the development would enable Pakistan to play a more effective role in discussions on global economic challenges and the interests of developing nations.

headline: Kamran Akmal praises NCA development work, welcomes modern facilities for young cricketers
description: Former Pakistan Test wicketkeeper Kamran Akmal has visited the National Cricket Academy (NCA), where Director of High Performance Aaqib Javed briefed him on
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Former Pakistan Test wicketkeeper Kamran Akmal has visited the National Cricket Academy (NCA), where Director of High Performance Aaqib Javed briefed him on the academy’s departments, ongoing infrastructure projects and player development initiatives.

During the visit, Akmal was given an overview of the improvements being made at the academy and the modern training facilities being introduced to help players sharpen their skills.

He also inspected the advanced bowling machine at the Bob Woolmer Indoor School and appreciated the extensive development work underway at the Lahore City Cricket Association (LCCA) Ground.

Speaking on the occasion, Akmal said he was pleased to see the professional approach being adopted towards cricket development and expressed hope that these efforts would deliver positive results for Pakistan cricket.

He said providing young cricketers with quality facilities and a supportive environment would help them receive better training and develop their skills before progressing to represent their regions and departments.

Akmal also welcomed the establishment of a biomechanics laboratory at the NCA and the construction of modern dressing rooms at the LCCA Ground.

He said it was encouraging to see development initiatives taking place at different levels, adding that the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) was extending full support to the process. He stressed that such facilities were particularly important for Pakistan cricket at this stage, with greater attention being directed towards nurturing emerging players.

Aaqib Javed, meanwhile, said 19 different pitches had been prepared at the LCCA Ground, enabling cricketers to train in varied playing conditions and work on improving their performance.

He added that a fresh practice wicket was prepared at the National Cricket Academy every Monday, giving players the opportunity to experience different conditions during the following five days.

Javed further said a Level One coaching course had been launched for the most promising Under-15 players, with the dual objective of developing future cricketers and preparing young coaches.

He also announced that the PCB would soon inaugurate a High Performance Centre in Peshawar, a move expected to create more opportunities for improving cricket infrastructure and developing players across the country.

headline: Pakistan’s 10 major gas fields hold 10.6 TCF in remaining reserves, oil fields 105 million barrels
description: Pakistan’s 10 largest gas fields hold 10.605 trillion cubic feet (TCF) of remaining recoverable reserves, while its 10 major oil fields contain an
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan’s 10 largest gas fields hold 10.605 trillion cubic feet (TCF) of remaining recoverable reserves, while its 10 major oil fields contain an estimated 105 million barrels, according to official figures presented in the National Assembly.

The data, provided by the Petroleum Division and available with Wealth Pakistan, offers an overview of the country’s remaining hydrocarbon resources and the government’s measures to increase domestic exploration and production.

The 10 major gas fields had combined original recoverable reserves of 43.358 TCF. Of this volume, 32.753 TCF had been extracted by June 30, 2026, leaving 10.605 TCF available for recovery.

Mari HRL, located in Ghotki district, has the largest remaining gas reserves at 2.777 TCF. It is followed by Uch in Dera Bugti, with 2.551 TCF.

Kandara in Sukkur holds 1.858 TCF of remaining reserves, while Mari Ghazij in Ghotki has 1.723 TCF.

Sui, one of Pakistan’s oldest and most prominent gas-producing fields, has 621 billion cubic feet (BCF) of recoverable reserves left. Against its original recoverable reserves of 12.655 TCF, cumulative production had reached 12.034 TCF by June 30, 2026.

The other major gas fields include Qadirpur in Ghotki, with 603 BCF of remaining reserves; Kandhkot in Kashmore, with 355 BCF; Sawan in Khairpur, with 83 BCF; Bhit in Dadu, with 23 BCF; and Zamzama, also in Dadu, with 11 BCF.

The 10 largest oil fields had combined original recoverable reserves of 567 million barrels. Of these, 462 million barrels had been produced, leaving 105 million barrels yet to be recovered.

Bargzai in Kohat district has the highest remaining oil reserves, estimated at 49 million barrels, followed by Pashaki/Pashaki North in Hyderabad with 11 million barrels.

Nashpa in Karak, Adhi in Rawalpindi and Dhurnal in Attock each hold around nine million barrels of remaining recoverable oil reserves.

Other fields include Kumar in Hyderabad with eight million barrels, Makori East in Karak with six million barrels, Balkassar in Chakwal with two million barrels and Meyal in Attock with one million barrels. No remaining recoverable reserves have been recorded for Dhokian in Attock.

To strengthen domestic energy supplies and address the decline in local production, the Petroleum Division has introduced several policy and exploration measures intended to attract investment and speed up the development of new hydrocarbon resources.

In October 2026, Pakistan held an offshore exploration bidding round after a gap of nearly 20 years. The process resulted in the award of 23 exploration blocks to local and international oil and gas companies.

The government has also held five onshore bidding rounds over the past three years, awarding 46 blocks for exploration and production activities.

Meanwhile, a detailed high-resolution basin study is underway to evaluate Pakistan’s hydrocarbon potential and identify new areas for exploration and development.

On the policy side, the Council of Common Interests approved the Tight Gas Policy 2024 in February 2024. The policy introduced additional pricing incentives compared with those available under the Petroleum Policy 2012 to encourage investment in tight gas resources.

Changes to the Petroleum Policy 2012 have also offered further incentives to exploration and production companies. These include the option to shift to the revised policy, access to Zone-I(F) incentives for existing licence holders and extensions in lease periods until commercial production begins.

Under the third-party gas sale framework, exploration and production companies can sell up to 35 per cent of gas from discoveries to third parties through competitive bidding, giving them another route to commercialise their resources.

The measures have coincided with increased exploration activity during the fiscal year 2025-26. Oil and gas companies drilled 58 exploratory and development wells during the period, resulting in 18 discoveries.

The reserves replacement ratio reached 2.64 for oil and 1.95 for gas, indicating that additions to recoverable reserves were higher than the quantities extracted during the year.

Exploration and production activities also contributed around 300 million cubic feet per day of natural gas and 16,000 barrels per day of crude oil to Pakistan’s domestic production system during FY2025-26.

headline: KP police to receive drones, anti-drone systems and armoured vehicles, says IG
description: Inspector General of Police Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Zulfiqar Hameed has announced plans to equip the provincial police with modern security equipment, including
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Inspector General of Police Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Zulfiqar Hameed has announced plans to equip the provincial police with modern security equipment, including drones, anti-drone systems, bulletproof vehicles and armoured personnel carriers (APCs).

The police chief said the department was also prioritising the expansion of Safe City projects to 12 districts across the province, with work progressing rapidly in Dera Ismail Khan, Bannu and Lakki Marwat.

“The work has been rapidly ongoing in Dera Ismail Khan, Bannu and Lakki Marwat,” IG Police said.

He added that efforts were underway to complete the Safe City projects in these three districts within a year.

Hameed further said that new police stations and police posts were being constructed in five northern districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as part of efforts to improve the department’s infrastructure and strengthen security arrangements.

headline: Surveillance drone crashes into outer wall of Lahore CTD headquarters
description: A surveillance drone crashed into the outer wall of the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) headquarters in Lahore late Saturday night, prompting concern among
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A surveillance drone crashed into the outer wall of the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) headquarters in Lahore late Saturday night, prompting concern among security personnel at the facility.

According to police, the incident took place at around 12:30am when the drone approached the headquarters from the direction of Jallo Mor.

Officials said the device struck the building’s outer wall before falling to the ground. The drone, described as a sophisticated surveillance device, was reportedly being used to monitor the premises of the CTD headquarters.

Security personnel recovered the drone and took it into custody. Its cameras and battery lights were still functioning when it was found. The bomb disposal squad subsequently inspected the device and declared it safe.

Police suspected that unidentified individuals had directed the drone towards the CTD headquarters with alleged terrorist intentions.

Authorities said the incident was being investigated from all possible angles. Meanwhile, the security team at the CTD headquarters has submitted an application to Harbanspura Police Station, seeking legal action over the incident.

headline: School van fares in twin cities rise by up to 40pc, adding to parents’ financial burden
description: School van and private transport operators in Rawalpindi and Islamabad have raised monthly fares by as much as 40 per cent following the recent increase in
author: APP
article_text:
School van and private transport operators in Rawalpindi and Islamabad have raised monthly fares by as much as 40 per cent following the recent increase in petrol prices amid tensions in the Middle East, placing additional financial pressure on parents.

Parents said transporters were demanding an extra Rs2,000 to Rs4,000 per month without any apparent regulatory oversight, even for school journeys covering distances of just three to five kilometres.

Sidra, a mother of two, said the monthly transport fee for her children had increased despite their school being only a short drive from home.

“My children go to a school in F-7, just 10 minutes away from our home in G-10, but the van driver has increased the fee from Rs 6000 to Rs 8,000, citing petrol hike”.

She said the government was providing a fuel subsidy for vehicles with engines up to 800cc, questioning the justification for such a steep increase in transport charges.

“The are already paying heavy school fees. This additional transport cost is unbearable for a middle-class family,” she added.

Another parent, Abdul Hanan, criticised van operators for using rising fuel prices to justify higher charges.

“They are using the petrol hike as an excuse. They charge full fee even during summer and winter vacations and there is no one to ask them.”

Transport operators, however, defended the revised fares, saying higher operating expenses had left them with little choice.

“Beside petrol , we have to pay for CNG, maintenance, and traffic challans. How can we operate in old fares? If we don’t increase, we will have to park the vans,” one operator said.

He maintained that the increase was necessary to keep the service running, citing fuel expenses, drivers’ salaries and commissions paid to schools.

“Parents think we earn a lot, but after deducting fuel, driver salary and school commission, we are left with very little. We have only increased Rs 1,500 which is justified,” he stated.

headline: The Material Enabling New Possibilities Across Industries
description: Many industrial innovations begin with materials rather than finished products. Nonwoven fabrics are a strong example. Their ability to be engineered across
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Many industrial innovations begin with materials rather than finished products.

Nonwoven fabrics are a strong example. Their ability to be engineered across different weights, structures, and performance requirements makes them relevant to industries as varied as hygiene, automotive, agriculture, bedding, retail, and packaging.

In Pakistan, Master Nonwoven has been part of this manufacturing landscape since 2002, developing local capability around a material category that continues to evolve with changing industrial needs.

Supporting Diverse Industrial Applications Unlike conventional woven fabrics, nonwovens can be manufactured in different weights, structures, and compositions to meet specific industrial requirements.

Master Nonwoven's product portfolio includes spunbond and meltblown fabrics, multilayer nonwoven materials, laminated fabrics, and polyester wadding and fiberfill. These materials serve a wide range of applications, from personal hygiene and protective products to automotive components, agriculture, bedding, and packaging.

Each category offers different properties depending on its intended use. Spun bond fabrics are widely used in hygiene, agriculture, and packaging, while multilayer structures can be developed for more specific performance requirements. Polyester wadding and fiberfill provide cushioning and filling solutions for bedding and other applications.

This diversity lets manufacturers choose materials based on required strength, weight, softness, and functionality, making nonwovens a versatile solution across industries.

From Specification to Application The value of nonwoven manufacturing lies in the ability to translate technical specifications into practical applications.

GSM, or grams per square metre, is one of the key considerations. It helps determine the weight and suitability of a material for a particular use.

A broader range of GSM and colour options therefore gives manufacturers greater flexibility when developing or modifying products.

Master Nonwoven supports this through one of the widest locally available ranges of GSM and colour options, helping serve requirements across different industrial categories.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Master Nonwoven (@masternonwoven)

Capability Behind Product Development Material flexibility needs to be supported by consistent production.

Master Nonwoven operates with an annual production capacity of 24,000 metric tonnes, supported by Italian-engineered production lines.

Its production setup is complemented by an in-house laboratory for quality control and quality assurance, along with end-to-end quality tracking across the manufacturing process.

For industrial customers, these systems are important because product development does not end with the first production run. Consistency across repeated cycles is equally critical.

The company also holds OEKO-TEX, ISO and CE certifications, supporting its focus on recognised manufacturing and quality standards.

New Uses Are Continuing to Emerge The role of nonwoven materials is continuing to expand as industries reassess product design, material efficiency and application requirements.

The COVID-19 period highlighted their importance in hygiene and protective products, while agriculture, automotive and personal care continue to remain significant areas of use.

Packaging is also creating new possibilities, particularly across reusable shopping solutions and alternative material formats.

Master Nonwoven also offers oxo-biodegradable material options where these specifications are relevant to customer requirements.

Materials That Enable What Comes Next As industries develop new products and refine existing ones, material capability becomes an important part of innovation.

Nonwovens offer manufacturers the flexibility to respond to different functional, technical and commercial requirements without being confined to a single type of application.

For Pakistan’s industrial sector, continued investment in this capability can support not only local manufacturing, but also the development of products designed around changing market needs.

In that sense, the importance of nonwovens lies less in how visible they are and more in what they enable.

headline: Govt expands free hepatitis C screening and treatment programme to GB, AJK
description: Free hepatitis C screening, diagnostic testing and treatment services have been introduced in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) under the
author: APP
article_text:
Free hepatitis C screening, diagnostic testing and treatment services have been introduced in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) under the Prime Minister’s National Programme for the Elimination of Hepatitis C.

According to official sources, three screening centres have been set up in Gilgit-Baltistan and six in AJK to help residents access testing and treatment without charge.

The Ministry of National Health Services has urged people in both regions to visit their nearest designated centres and benefit from the programme. It has also encouraged residents to spread awareness among their families and communities.

Under the initiative, patients can receive free initial screening, PCR diagnostic tests valued at around Rs8,000 and treatment worth between Rs34,000 and Rs68,000, with all services provided free of cost to eligible individuals.

Hepatitis C remains a significant public health concern, with an estimated 60 million people affected worldwide and around 11 million in Pakistan.

The virus can spread through contaminated blood, unsafe injections and infected shaving equipment. If left untreated, the infection can cause serious liver damage and increase the risk of complications, including liver cancer.

The health ministry has stressed that hepatitis C is curable and that early screening, timely diagnosis and completion of treatment are essential to prevent serious health complications and limit the spread of the infection.

Residents seeking further information about screening centres and treatment services can contact the government's toll-free helpline at 1166.

The expansion to Gilgit-Baltistan and AJK follows the introduction of the programme in Islamabad. The government plans to extend free screening, diagnosis and treatment services to other parts of the country as part of its efforts to eliminate hepatitis C nationwide.

According to official sources, three screening centres have been set up in Gilgit-Baltistan and six in AJK to help residents access testing and treatment without charge.

The Ministry of National Health Services has urged people in both regions to visit their nearest designated centres and benefit from the programme. It has also encouraged residents to spread awareness among their families and communities.

Under the initiative, patients can receive free initial screening, PCR diagnostic tests valued at around Rs8,000 and treatment worth between Rs34,000 and Rs68,000, with all services provided free of cost to eligible individuals.

Hepatitis C remains a significant public health concern, with an estimated 60 million people affected worldwide and around 11 million in Pakistan.

The virus can spread through contaminated blood, unsafe injections and infected shaving equipment. If left untreated, the infection can cause serious liver damage and increase the risk of complications, including liver cancer.

The health ministry has stressed that hepatitis C is curable and that early screening, timely diagnosis and completion of treatment are essential to prevent serious health complications and limit the spread of the infection.

Residents seeking further information about screening centres and treatment services can contact the government's toll-free helpline at 1166.

The expansion to Gilgit-Baltistan and AJK follows the introduction of the programme in Islamabad. The government plans to extend free screening, diagnosis and treatment services to other parts of the country as part of its efforts to eliminate hepatitis C nationwide.

headline: Pakistan welcomes US offer to facilitate dialogue with Afghanistan, links talks to action against militants
description: Pakistan has welcomed the United States’ willingness to help ease tensions between Islamabad and Kabul, saying it is ready to support sincere diplomatic
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan has welcomed the United States’ willingness to help ease tensions between Islamabad and Kabul, saying it is ready to support sincere diplomatic efforts by Washington and other friendly countries to facilitate dialogue with Afghanistan.

According to a statement by the Foreign Office spokesperson in Islamabad, meaningful negotiations would require a clear commitment from the Afghan Taliban authorities to take concrete action against militant groups operating from Afghan territory.

The spokesperson said Kabul must take effective and verifiable measures against the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Fitna al-Khawarij (FAK), Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), Fitna al-Hindustan (FAH) and other militant organisations.

Pakistan considers addressing the presence and activities of these groups a key requirement for creating an environment in which productive discussions between the two countries can take place.

Reaffirming Islamabad’s position, the spokesperson said Pakistan remained committed to constructive engagement with Afghanistan. However, any dialogue must result in practical progress towards resolving the country’s legitimate security concerns.

The response followed remarks by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who said Washington had heard Pakistan’s concerns about militant attacks originating from Afghan territory and was willing to play a constructive role in reducing tensions between the neighbouring countries.

Pakistan’s position reflects its continued call for diplomatic engagement with Kabul alongside verifiable action against militant groups, which it says is necessary for lasting regional peace and stability.

headline: Global trade outlook improves as AI investment drives demand for technology
description: Strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is improving the global trade outlook, as rising demand for semiconductors, servers and other
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is improving the global trade outlook, as rising demand for semiconductors, servers and other advanced technologies supports international commerce and creates new opportunities for developing economies to participate in the expanding digital economy.

The World Trade Organization (WTO) has raised its 2026 global merchandise trade volume growth forecast to 3.9% from 1.9%, citing resilient supply chains and stronger-than-expected investment in AI-related infrastructure as important factors behind the improved outlook.

According to the WTO's October Global Trade Outlook and Statistics, AI-enabling goods accounted for 47% of the increase in the value of global merchandise trade during the first half of 2026, while trade in these products expanded by 67% year-on-year. The growth helped offset disruptions in energy and transport markets caused by the Middle East conflict, as international supply chains adjusted through alternative suppliers, ports and trade routes.

The WTO expects AI-related investment to remain an important driver of merchandise trade through 2027. However, participation in the emerging AI supply chain remains highly concentrated, with the world's 10 largest traders of AI-enabling goods accounting for approximately 85% of global exports and 80% of imports in 2025.

Muhammad Hafeez, founder and CEO of Nexa Robots Pvt Ltd, told Wealth Pakistan that the growing demand for AI infrastructure could create opportunities for developing economies beyond advanced semiconductor manufacturing, particularly in software development, industrial automation, systems integration and technical services.

“Investment in data centres, chips and servers is exceptionally strong right now, but spending of this scale tends to move in cycles,” he said. Hafeez explained that although the current pace of AI infrastructure investment might eventually moderate, demand for computing, automation and practical AI applications was likely to continue expanding.

He said the production of advanced semiconductors and servers would probably remain concentrated in a limited number of economies due to the substantial capital, technological expertise, and manufacturing scale required. However, the wider adoption of AI could create opportunities for businesses capable of integrating imported equipment, adapting software and providing maintenance and technical support.

According to Hafeez, developing economies could benefit from the global AI investment boom by building capabilities around technologies they import rather than attempting to replicate the most capital-intensive segments of the industry. He cited the example of Nexa Robots, which combines imported robotics hardware with locally developed software, AI applications and systems integration. The company also works with Chinese technology and manufacturing partners to develop robotics solutions adapted to Pakistan's requirements.

Hafeez said Pakistan could develop expertise in robotics and automation through system integration, software adaptation, deployment, maintenance and technical support. Selective manufacturing of components could also become commercially viable as domestic demand for automation technologies expands, he added.

He emphasised that predictable customs and tax treatment for automation equipment and spare parts, accessible financing or leasing arrangements and practical technical training would help Pakistani businesses adopt advanced technologies more effectively. The expansion of AI-related trade is also creating opportunities beyond computing hardware, as the technology requires supporting investment in electricity, data centres, connectivity, software and digital services.

Kazim Ullah, Software Engineer, Technology Educator, Co-founder of Devspire Solutions and Mentor of the IT & Robotics Society at City University Peshawar, told Wealth Pakistan that the economic impact of AI extended across multiple sectors. He said the development and deployment of AI systems required investment in energy infrastructure, data management, computing facilities and digital connectivity alongside semiconductors and servers.

This expanding ecosystem could create opportunities for developing economies to participate in international technology markets through specialised services and applications, even without producing advanced computing hardware.

However, Kazim cautioned that the sustainability of the current AI investment boom would depend on whether the technology delivered measurable productivity improvements and commercially useful applications. He said developing countries did not necessarily need to manufacture advanced semiconductors or build large foundational AI models to benefit from the growing international demand for AI technologies.

Opportunities also existed in AI-enabled software, industrial automation, cloud services, data management, specialised applications and technology-enabled business services, he explained. For Pakistan, these activities could provide practical avenues for developing domestic technological expertise, improving business efficiency and expanding technology-related exports.

Kazim said developing economies should identify areas where they could realistically create economic value while investing in reliable electricity, digital infrastructure, technical education, research and affordable computing resources. He also stressed the importance of collaboration among universities, businesses and research institutions to strengthen technical capabilities and accelerate the commercial application of AI.

Wider AI skills development across manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, education and finance could help businesses adopt new technologies and improve productivity, he added. The growing international demand for AI infrastructure highlights a broader transformation in global trade, with advanced computing equipment and related technologies becoming increasingly important components of merchandise flows.

However, the WTO's figures also show that much of this trade remains concentrated among a relatively small number of economies, making technological capabilities and industrial competitiveness important factors in determining which countries benefit.

For Pakistan and other developing economies, the opportunity lies in moving beyond importing AI equipment towards developing the software, technical expertise and industrial applications required to create domestic economic value. The longer-term benefits of the global AI investment boom will depend on whether developing economies can translate access to advanced technologies into stronger productivity, specialised services, industrial innovation and competitive technology-related exports.

Hafeez explained that although the current pace of AI infrastructure investment might eventually moderate, demand for computing, automation and practical AI applications was likely to continue expanding.

He said the production of advanced semiconductors and servers would probably remain concentrated in a limited number of economies due to the substantial capital, technological expertise, and manufacturing scale required.

However, the wider adoption of AI could create opportunities for businesses capable of integrating imported equipment, adapting software and providing maintenance and technical support.

According to Hafeez, developing economies could benefit from the global AI investment boom by building capabilities around technologies they import rather than attempting to replicate the most capital-intensive segments of the industry.

He cited the example of Nexa Robots, which combines imported robotics hardware with locally developed software, AI applications and systems integration. The company also works with Chinese technology and manufacturing partners to develop robotics solutions adapted to Pakistan's requirements.

Hafeez said Pakistan could develop expertise in robotics and automation through system integration, software adaptation, deployment, maintenance and technical support.

Selective manufacturing of components could also become commercially viable as domestic demand for automation technologies expands, he added.

He emphasised that predictable customs and tax treatment for automation equipment and spare parts, accessible financing or leasing arrangements and practical technical training would help Pakistani businesses adopt advanced technologies more effectively.

The expansion of AI-related trade is also creating opportunities beyond computing hardware, as the technology requires supporting investment in electricity, data centres, connectivity, software and digital services.

Kazim Ullah, Software Engineer, Technology Educator, Co-founder of Devspire Solutions and Mentor of the IT & Robotics Society at City University Peshawar, told Wealth Pakistan that the economic impact of AI extended across multiple sectors.

He said the development and deployment of AI systems required investment in energy infrastructure, data management, computing facilities and digital connectivity alongside semiconductors and servers.

This expanding ecosystem could create opportunities for developing economies to participate in international technology markets through specialised services and applications, even without producing advanced computing hardware.

However, Kazim cautioned that the sustainability of the current AI investment boom would depend on whether the technology delivered measurable productivity improvements and commercially useful applications.

He said developing countries did not necessarily need to manufacture advanced semiconductors or build large foundational AI models to benefit from the growing international demand for AI technologies.

Opportunities also existed in AI-enabled software, industrial automation, cloud services, data management, specialised applications and technology-enabled business services, he explained.

For Pakistan, these activities could provide practical avenues for developing domestic technological expertise, improving business efficiency and expanding technology-related exports.

Kazim said developing economies should identify areas where they could realistically create economic value while investing in reliable electricity, digital infrastructure, technical education, research and affordable computing resources.

He also stressed the importance of collaboration among universities, businesses and research institutions to strengthen technical capabilities and accelerate the commercial application of AI.

Wider AI skills development across manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, education and finance could help businesses adopt new technologies and improve productivity, he added.

The growing international demand for AI infrastructure highlights a broader transformation in global trade, with advanced computing equipment and related technologies becoming increasingly important components of merchandise flows.

However, the WTO's figures also show that much of this trade remains concentrated among a relatively small number of economies, making technological capabilities and industrial competitiveness important factors in determining which countries benefit.

For Pakistan and other developing economies, the opportunity lies in moving beyond importing AI equipment towards developing the software, technical expertise and industrial applications required to create domestic economic value.

The longer-term benefits of the global AI investment boom will depend on whether developing economies can translate access to advanced technologies into stronger productivity, specialised services, industrial innovation and competitive technology-related exports.
